Meets all inclusion criteria: task-based fMRI of children using cognitive reappraisal to regulate emotional responses to visual (sad) stimuli, and reports task-related brain activation (PFC, amygdala). Task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal (up- and down-regulation) using visual stimuli (angry faces) in patients with depression and healthy controls; reports task-related neural activation (amygdala, insula, prefrontal regions). No exclusion criteria met.

Title and abstract state this is an fMRI study of emotion regulation in bipolar disorder type I with human clinical participants. Include for full-text review to confirm task details and reported activations.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study in healthy humans instructed to use cognitive reappraisal (an emotion regulation task) and reports task-related brain activation results (dmPFC response). Abstract reports an empirical task-based fMRI study of human healthy participants using cognitive reappraisal to regulate emotional responses to visual stimuli and reports task-related brain activation; no exclusion criteria are met.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation) in human participants and reports task-related brain activation/effective connectivity (DCM) results. No exclusion criteria are met; inclusion criteria I1–I4 are satisfied based on the abstract.

Abstract indicates a study of neural activation during emotion regulation in adolescents with and without suicidal ideation, but does not specify stimulus modality (visual) or full task details. Inclusion uncertain from abstract-only evidence, so include for full-text review.

Study reports task-based fMRI of human participants using a reappraisal (detachment-from-threat) emotion-regulation task and presents reappraisal-related brain activation results (shifts in lateral frontal cortex). Meets inclusion criteria I1–I4; no exclusion criteria apparent.

fMRI study examining neural substrates of emotion regulation in women with PMDD; abstract implies a task probing emotion regulation but does not specify stimuli type, regulation instructions, or presence of a control group. No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion not met / not demonstrated: I2 (participants performing an emotion-regulation task of visual stimuli as required by the review objective). Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study where MDD participants performed a voluntary emotion regulation strategy (recalling negative autobiographical memories) with BOLD contrasts reported; includes clinical and control groups. Excluded because the study examined internal self-referential awareness/introspection (no mention of regulating responses to externally presented visual stimuli), which does not meet the review objective. Inclusion met: I1, I3, I4. Inclusion not met/not demonstrated: I2 (emotion regulation of responses to visual stimuli or comparable reappraisal of visual stimuli). Exclusion criteria E1/E2 not met.

Task-based fMRI fear conditioning/extinction protocol constitutes a task involving viewing emotional (fear) stimuli (without instructed regulation) and reports task-related brain activation in human participants. Include for full-text review to confirm task details.

Title/abstract indicate a task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal (an emotion regulation strategy) in human participants (girls at high risk for depression) and report neural activation; thus inclusion criteria I1, I2, I3, and I4 are met. Abstract provides insufficient methodological detail to confirm inclusion: it does not state whether task-based fMRI was used, whether participants performed an instructed emotion-regulation task during fMRI, or whether task-related brain activation results are reported. No exclusion criteria are met in the abstract. Include for full-text review to assess I1–I4.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study using an affect-labeling emotion-regulation task in human participants (social phobia groups and healthy controls) and reports task-related amygdala and prefrontal activation/connectivity; no exclusion criteria are met.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal in depressed adolescents, reporting task-related brain activation differences; meets inclusion criteria for task-based fMRI, emotion regulation (reappraisal), applicable participant groups (clinical adolescents with control comparison), and reports activation results. Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation), reports task-related brain activation results, and involves human participants. Abstract implies brain imaging with reported activation of emotion-regulation neurocircuits but does not specify whether participants performed an emotion regulation task or whether humans were tested. Insufficient information to confirm all inclusion criteria, so include for full-text review.

Task-based fMRI study of human participants performing cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation). Abstract reports task-related brain activation results (amygdala, prefrontal) during regulation. No exclusion criteria met.

This is a task-based fMRI study in humans with generalized social anxiety disorder performing an emotion regulation task (attention regulation of negative self-beliefs) and reporting task-related neural activation results comparing MBSR vs aerobic exercise. Abstract reports comparisons of gambling disorder patients and healthy controls using brain activation measures of emotion regulation, indicating a task-based fMRI investigation of emotion regulation in human participants. Include for full-text review to confirm task specifics and contrasts.

Event-related task-based fMRI with healthy human participants performing a cognitive control task over emotional stimuli (CECT). Although not an explicit instructed regulation task, the study assesses cognitive control of emotion (allowed). No exclusion criteria met.

Study used diffusion tensor imaging (structural MRI) and self-report measures, not task-based fMRI; participants did not perform an emotion regulation task during scanning and no task-related activation results are reported. Exclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion criteria not met or not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (participants performing an emotion regulation task), I4 (reports task-related brain activation results).

Abstract reports a task-based rt-fMRI study in humans training emotion regulation using a 'reality check' strategy during presentation of emotional pictures, includes healthy participants and a control group, and reports task-related activation and connectivity (amygdala down-regulation). No exclusion criteria are met.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study of human participants performing emotion regulation of negative visual stimuli, examining SSRI effects and 5-HTTLPR moderation and reporting neural (fMRI) outcomes. Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation) in adolescent girls with PTSD and reports task-related amygdala functional connectivity changes associated with symptom reduction. This meets inclusion criteria I1–I4 and no exclusion criteria are indicated in the abstract.

No active emotion-regulation task: study measured dispositional cognitive reappraisal and related it to fear conditioning but did not instruct participants to regulate during the fMRI task. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion not met: I2 (participants performing an emotion regulation task). Exclusion criteria: none met.

Abstract describes an empirical task-based rtfMRI neurofeedback study in healthy human participants targeting hippocampal activation to enhance emotion regulation. Exclusion criteria are not met.
