Full-text review needed to confirm relevance to the meta-analysis objective.

Abstract indicates an fMRI task involving observation of risk-taking actions and suggests investigation of emotion-related processing; it is unclear whether participants actively regulated emotions or merely viewed stimuli. Task-based fMRI, human participants, and task-related activation are implied, so include for full-text review to determine presence of regulation instructions.

No task-based emotion regulation paradigm reported: study uses resting-state fMRI examining inflammation and rsFC. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human participants implied). Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I1 (not task-based fMRI), I2 (no emotion regulation task), I4 (no task-related activation reported).

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study using cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation) in human children (clinical MDD history and controls) and reports task-related functional connectivity results; no exclusion criteria met.

No task-based fMRI or emotion-regulation task: the study is a resting-state fMRI investigation and does not report task-related activation. Exclusion criteria: none met. Inclusion criteria met: none clearly satisfied. Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I1 (not task-based), I2 (no emotion regulation task/strategy reported), I4 (no task-related activation results), I3 not demonstrated (clinical sample implied but control group not reported).

Title and abstract indicate a task-based fMRI study of emotion regulation in adolescent major depressive disorder, reporting amygdala response and functional connectivity consistent with task-related brain activation. This meets I1–I4. No exclusion criteria are indicated in the abstract. Full-text review warranted to confirm details (e.g., control group reporting).

Study reports task-based fMRI in human participants performing cognitive reappraisal (watch vs reappraise) with clinical (SAD) and healthy control groups, and reports task-related brain activation/connectivity results. No exclusion criteria are met.

Abstract describes an empirical task-based fMRI study in humans using cognitive reappraisal to regulate emotion, reports task-related brain activation results, and includes clinical and control groups. No exclusion criteria apply.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study in which human participants cognitively up-regulated (engaged) positive-social emotions from a first-person perspective and reports fMRI activation and effective connectivity results. This meets inclusion criteria I1–I4 and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text review recommended to extract details.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation) during peer-rejection in depressed and non-depressed adolescents and reports functional connectivity/brain activation findings. This meets inclusion criteria I1, I2, I3 and I4 and no exclusion criteria are evident. Include for full-text review.

Task-based fMRI with healthy human participants instructed to regulate (expressive suppression) and imitate emotional facial expressions while viewing dynamic visual stimuli; reports task-related brain activation. Meets I1–I4. No exclusion criteria met.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation) in healthy human participants, with voxelwise task-related brain activation results (PFC and amygdala). This satisfies inclusion criteria I1–I4 and no exclusion criteria are met based on the abstract.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study in smokers using cognitive reappraisal to regulate craving (emotion regulation). It addresses brain activation (dACC) related to regulation, meeting inclusion for full-text review. The abstract does not explicitly report activation results, so full text is needed to confirm I4.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study of human participants performing explicit emotion regulation (up-/downregulation) while viewing negative images, reports task-related brain activation (VLPFC, amygdala), and includes clinical groups and healthy controls. No exclusion criteria are met.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study with human participants performing an active cognitive emotion regulation task (cognitive reappraisal), includes both depressed patients and healthy controls, and reports whole-brain activation and connectivity results relevant to regulation vs. passive viewing; meets all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are met.

Meets all inclusion criteria: task-based fMRI of human participants performing cognitive reappraisal (down-/up-regulation) of visual/episodic negative images, reports task-related brain activation results. No exclusion criteria met.

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion IDs not met or not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI not stated in abstract), I2 (no evidence participants performed an emotion-regulation task on visual stimuli—study involves mood induction and pain), I4 (task-related brain activation results not reported in abstract). Therefore excluded from this review.

E1: This paper is a review/meta-analysis and does not present original task-based fMRI data. Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met/demonstrated: I1 (not an original task-based fMRI study), I2 (no original human participants performing an emotion-regulation task), I3 (no participant groups reported as original data), I4 (no original task-related activation results).

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study in humans using a cognitive reappraisal emotion-regulation task, reports task-related brain activation and connectivity results, and includes healthy adult participants. All inclusion criteria are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study (I1) where human participants (adult females) performed emotion regulation tasks (attend, expressive suppression, cognitive reappraisal) to negative images (I2, I3) and presents task-related brain activation and connectivity results (I4). No exclusion criteria are met. Abstract provides sufficient information for inclusion in full-text review.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study in adult humans using instructed cognitive reappraisal (Social-Reg) versus look, reporting task-related brain activation contrasts and associations with behavior; meets inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are evident.

Task-based fMRI with human participants instructed to regulate responses to visual food stimuli using cognitive reappraisal, suppression and up-/down-regulation; reports task-related brain activation results. Fits meta-analysis objective of regulation of emotional/affective responses to visual stimuli.

No emotion regulation instruction reported (I2 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), I4 (task-related brain activation results). Exclusion criteria met: none. Therefore excluded because participants viewed stimuli without performing a defined emotion-regulation task required for the review.

Task-based fMRI in human participants comparing emotion-regulation-related instructions (permit/accept vs view) during viewing of unpleasant and neutral visual stimuli; reports subjective ratings and task-related brain activation (amygdala). Meets I1–I4 and no exclusion criteria apply.

Task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal in adult human participants that reports task-related brain activation (PFC and amygdala). The abstract meets inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are apparent, so include for full-text review.

Abstract reports neural activity during explicit emotion regulation in humans and links it to resting-state vmHRV, implying a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation study that reports task-related brain activation. Meets inclusion criteria I1-I4; no exclusion criteria met.

Meets inclusion criteria: task-based fMRI of cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation) in human participants (children/adolescents with ASD and TD controls) and reports task-related brain activation and connectivity results. No exclusion criteria met.

Task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation) in human participants; reports task-related brain activation (prefrontal, cingulate, occipital, subcortical) across experiments, meeting inclusion criteria for meta-analysis.

Exclusion E1 applies: this paper is a meta-analysis (no original human data). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met/demonstrated: I1 (not a task-based fMRI study), I2 (does not involve an emotion regulation task), I3 (no original human participants reported), I4 (does not report original task-related activation results).

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation) using standardized negative scripts in human participants, with clinical and control groups and task-related brain activation results. All inclusion criteria are met; include for full-text review to confirm stimulus modality (script-driven vs. visual) and extract activation contrasts.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that directly tests emotion regulation (reappraisal and suppression) while viewing negative pictures and reports neural activation results, satisfying the review objective and inclusion criteria.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study using cognitive reappraisal (distancing) in healthy human participants and presents task-related brain activation results (ventral striatum, fronto-parietal network). No exclusion criteria are met.

Abstract reports an empirical task-based fMRI study of an emotion regulation (ER) task in human participants (n=60) and presents task-related neural activation changes pre- to post-training. No exclusion criteria are met.

The study uses recall of an anger-inducing autobiographical memory (no visual stimuli), so it does not address the meta-analysis objective of regulating emotional responses to visual stimuli. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I1, I2, I3, I4. Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: regulation of emotional responses to visual stimuli (study uses autobiographical recall).

Task-based fMRI with human participants (N=10) performing emotion regulation tasks (reappraisal and affect labeling) and reporting task-related brain activation (amygdala, IFG). Tasks involve regulating emotional responses and fit the meta-analysis objective. No exclusion criteria met.

Study uses auditory stimuli (angry prosody) rather than visual stimuli required by the review objective, so it does not address the review's focus on regulation of visual emotions. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I1, I2, I3, I4. Inclusion IDs not met or not demonstrated: regulation of visual stimuli (modality requirement).

Abstract reports cognitive reappraisal of palatable food images in human participants across a BMI range and describes modulation of neural responsivity—matching emotion regulation of visual stimuli and task-related brain activation. The abstract does not explicitly state 'task-based fMRI', so include for full-text review to confirm imaging modality.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study in which SAD patients performed emotion-regulation tasks (breath-focused and distraction-focused attention) while reacting to negative self-beliefs and shows task-related brain activation changes (amygdala and attentional regions). It is unclear whether stimuli were visual and no control group is mentioned; insufficient information to exclude. Include for full-text review to confirm visual-stimuli requirement and presence/absence of separate control group.

Task-based model-based fMRI in human participants using cognitive emotion regulation (aversive conditioning with and without regulation), reporting prediction error-related and task-related neural activation. No exclusion criteria met.

Human task-based rtfMRI study reporting task-related activation and voluntary modulation of emotional states via neurofeedback. Abstract does not clearly state regulation of responses to visual stimuli or a view condition/comparison common in the review objective, so inclusion is uncertain from abstract alone — include for full-text review.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study using a film-based emotion regulation task in human adolescents/young adults and presents task-related neural activation results (prefrontal cortex, amygdala). No exclusion criteria are met.

Task-based fMRI study of emotion regulation (reappraisal/detachment) with passive viewing; includes clinical (AN) and age-matched control groups; reports behavioral arousal ratings and task-related fMRI activation results—meets all inclusion criteria.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (human clinical and control groups reported). Inclusion criteria not met or not demonstrated: I1 (not a task-based fMRI study; uses structural MRI/gray matter volume), I2 (participants did not perform an emotion regulation task), I4 (does not report task-related brain activation results). Therefore excluded based on failure to meet required inclusion criteria I1, I2, and I4.

Task-based real-time fMRI neurofeedback study in human adolescents (7–16) teaching up-/down-regulation of an emotion-regulation region (insula); reports task-related activation and connectivity. Unclear whether regulation targeted emotional responses to visual stimuli specifically, but meets broad emotion-regulation criteria and warrants full-text review.

Abstract reports a randomized, placebo-controlled task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation) in healthy adults and presents task-related activation and functional connectivity results (amygdala and dlPFC). No exclusion criteria are met from the abstract. Full-text review warranted to extract details.

Study reports a task-based fMRI experiment in healthy human (female) participants performing voluntary emotion regulation of emotional pictures and reports task-related brain activation results; matches I1, I2, I3, and I4. No exclusion criteria met.

Patient-only fMRI neurofeedback study (Patients n=10) with no separately reported control group in the abstract. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (participants performed an emotion regulation task—downregulation while viewing trauma words), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion criterion not met/not demonstrated: I3 (no control group reported for the patient sample). Exclusion criteria: none met (E1,E2 not applicable).

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study including an explicit cognitive emotion regulation task and an emotional Stroop, includes patient and control groups, and reports task-related brain activation (left supramarginal gyrus). No exclusion criteria met. Include for full-text review.

Task-based fMRI study (N=26) of primiparous mothers using distraction to regulate emotions in response to infant crying; reports reduced amygdala activation with regulation. Satisfies I1,I2,I3,I4. Stimulus modality appears auditory (infant crying) not visual, so relevance to the visual-stimulus meta-analysis objective is uncertain; include for full-text review.

Excluded because the study uses resting-state fMRI acquired before and after an emotion-regulation task rather than reporting task-based fMRI activation; therefore I1 (task-based fMRI) and I4 (task-related activation results) are not met. It meets I2 (participants performed an emotion regulation task) and I3 (clinical and control groups). No exclusion criteria apply.

Abstract reports a neuroanatomical MRI study of somatoform disorders with no mention of task-based fMRI, emotion regulation tasks, or task-related activation results. Inclusion criteria I1, I2, and I4 are not met; I3 (participant groups) is not demonstrated. No exclusion criteria (E1/E2) apply based on the abstract.

Task-based fMRI in humans comparing emotion regulation strategies (cognitive reappraisal and expressive suppression) to natural viewing of visual scenes; reports task-related brain activation results and manipulates stimulus valence and social content. Meets I1, I2, I3, I4; no exclusion criteria apparent.

No emotion-regulation task is reported in the abstract (I2 not met). The study is a task-based human fMRI experiment reporting task-evoked activation (I1 and I4 met). Participant details are not specified in abstract (I3 not demonstrated). No exclusion criteria (E1/E2) appear applicable.

Excluded because the study did not use task-based fMRI (I1 not met); it used magnetoencephalography and structural MRI. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (task involving inhibition of aversive socio-emotional stimuli), I3 (human participants—school-age children), I4 (reports task-related functional brain activity). Exclusion criteria met: none.

Abstract describes an fMRI study in adolescents examining brain responses/connectivity to emotional frustration (task-based fMRI, human participants, reports task-related brain activation/connectivity). It does not clearly state whether an explicit emotion-regulation instruction (reappraisal/distancing/etc.) was used, so I2 is uncertain; include for full-text review to verify.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study (I1) using cognitive emotion regulation/reappraisal during reward anticipation (I2) in healthy human participants (I3) and reports task-related brain activation results (DLPFC, putamen, PPI) (I4). No exclusion criteria are met; include for full-text review.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study in human participants (38 males) and reports task-related neural responses in emotion-regulation networks during virtual violent actions. It is unclear from the abstract whether participants were explicitly instructed to regulate their emotions (I2 not clearly demonstrated), so full-text is needed to confirm. I1, I3, and I4 are met based on the abstract; no exclusion criteria appear to apply.

Excluded because the study used olfactory (odor) stimuli rather than the visual-stimuli required by this meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I3 (human participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Exclusion criteria met: none (E1, E2 not applicable). Inclusion criteria not met or not demonstrated: does not meet the meta-analysis' stimulus-modality requirement (visual stimuli).

Meets all inclusion criteria: task-based fMRI (I1); participants performed an implicit emotion regulation task (I2); includes clinical SAD group and healthy controls reported separately (I3); reports task-related brain activation/connectivity results (PPI amygdala-vmPFC) and pre/post treatment changes (I4). No exclusion criteria are met based on abstract.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants with patient and control groups), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I2 — the study used a Monetary Incentive Delay task assessing reward/punishment processing, not an emotion-regulation task (no reappraisal/acceptance/instruction to regulate emotions).

This is a structural MRI/DTI study comparing gray matter volume and FA in children; it is NOT a task-based fMRI study and does not report task-related activation or any emotion regulation task. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion IDs not met: I1 (not task-based fMRI), I2 (no emotion-regulation task), I4 (no task-related brain activation results).

Abstract reports an fMRI study of older adults with amnestic MCI addressing affective regulation and frontal dysfunction, but does not specify a task-based emotion regulation paradigm or task-related activation results. Insufficient detail to confirm I1, I2, and I4 from the abstract alone, so include for full-text review.

Task-based fMRI with human participants (BPD patients and controls) reporting task-related brain activation/connectivity during viewing of negative vs neutral pictures with heat pain. Fits review objective (regulate or view without regulating). Abstract does not clearly state participants performed an explicit emotion regulation instruction (I2 unclear), so full-text review needed to confirm. Includes I1, I3, I4; no exclusion criteria met.

Randomized, placebo-controlled task-based fMRI in human participants assessing distraction as an emotion regulation strategy in PTSD patients and controls; reports task-related brain activation and functional connectivity results (thalamus, striatum, amygdala). Thus it meets I1–I4 and no exclusion criteria apply.

Task-based fMRI with human adults using instructed emotion regulation (increase/decrease negative responses) during a task; reports ACC activation and connectivity related to errors (task-related brain activation). Fits inclusion criteria I1-I4; no exclusion criteria met.

Study is excluded because it does not address the review objective: participants regulated emotion during autobiographical memory recall rather than in response to visual stimuli. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation via cognitive reappraisal), I3 (human participants), I4 (reports task-related activation). No exclusion criteria met (none).

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study where human participants used cognitive reappraisal to up- and downregulate emotional responses to visual threat-related stimuli; reports task-related brain activation (amygdala, prefrontal regions) and physiological/self-report measures. No exclusion criteria are met.

Abstract lacks key details: it does not state whether task-based fMRI was used, whether participants performed an explicit emotion regulation task, or whether task-related brain activation results are reported. Because inclusion cannot be determined from the abstract alone, include for full-text review to assess I1–I4.

Meets all inclusion criteria: task-based fMRI (I1), an implicit emotion-regulation/emotion-label task (I2), human adolescent participants (I3), and reports task-related brain activation and connectivity results (I4). No exclusion criteria met.

Task-based human fMRI study where smokers viewed emotionally evocative anti-smoking messages; reports task-related activations (amygdala, vmPFC) and a regulation-related brain pattern moderating responses. Fits I1 (task fMRI), I2 (viewing/regulating emotional stimuli), I3 (human participants), and I4 (task-related activation results). No exclusion criteria are met.

Abstract investigates neural correlates of emotion regulation in BPD with patient and control groups, satisfying I3. The abstract does not explicitly state task-based fMRI (I1), that participants performed a defined emotion-regulation task (I2), or that task-related brain activation results are reported (I4). No exclusion criteria are met. Insufficient detail to determine inclusion from abstract alone, so include for full-text review.

Task-based fMRI in healthy humans (n=18) using an emotion regulation task (reappraisal) and reporting task-related activations (vmPFC, amygdala). Abstract does not specify whether emotional stimuli were visual, so insufficient information to confirm the review's visual-stimulus requirement; include for full-text review to determine stimulus modality. No exclusion criteria met.

Study addresses emotion circuitry and regulation in human first-degree relatives but abstract does not specify whether a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation (view vs regulate) paradigm was used or whether task-related activation results are reported. Insufficient information to confirm I1, I2, and I4, but I3 (human participants) is met. Include for full-text review to determine eligibility.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study in humans (12 females, 12 males) performing emotion regulation (view vs regulate emotional responses to pictures) and reports task-related brain activation results. All inclusion criteria I1–I4 are met; no exclusion criteria apply. Include for full-text review.

Task-based fMRI in 40 healthy human participants viewing emotion-eliciting images while applying emotion regulation strategies (goal vs. implementation intentions). Abstract reports task-related brain activation (prefrontal regions, amygdala, OFC coupling). Meets inclusion criteria I1–I4; no exclusion criteria are met or suggested by the abstract.

Task-based fMRI study in human participants (spider-phobic patients) using cognitive reappraisal as an emotion regulation strategy and reporting fMRI activation related to regulation; fits I1–I4. No exclusion criteria are met in the abstract. Include for full-text review to extract task-related activation details.

Abstract indicates a neuroimaging study of emotional cue processing but does not specify task-based fMRI, whether participants performed an emotion-regulation or passive viewing task, or report task-related activation results. Information is insufficient to determine whether inclusion criteria I1, I2, and I4 are met. Include for full-text review to clarify methods and outcomes.

E1 (non-empirical conceptual/review article): abstract describes a conceptual model and does not report original human task-based fMRI data. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (human participants performing an emotion regulation task), I3 (participant groups reported), I4 (task-related brain activation results).

Task-based rtfMRI neurofeedback study in humans training down-regulation of amygdala during presentation of negative emotional faces using a regulation strategy ('reality checking'); reports task-related amygdala activation changes and compares to passive viewing; healthy participants. Meets inclusion criteria I1, I2, I3, I4; no exclusion criteria met.

Exclusion based on failure to meet inclusion criteria: Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human clinical participants). Inclusion IDs not met: I1 (not a task-based fMRI study; uses resting-state fMRI), I2 (no emotion regulation task during scanning), I4 (no task-related activation results reported; reports resting-state connectivity changes).

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study with human participants (45 women) who performed explicit reappraisal and an implicit placebo regulation while viewing disgusting visual stimuli; reports task-related brain activation and connectivity results. No exclusion criteria met. Include for full-text review.

Task-based fMRI study in humans reporting task-related brain activation during anticipation of emotional visual stimuli. Participants viewed (without explicit regulation) emotional pictures and anticipation was examined; fits meta-analysis objective of studies that regulate or view without regulating. Clinical and control groups reported separately. No exclusion criteria met.

Task-based fMRI with human participants performing an emotion regulation task (up-regulation of positive emotions to visual images), healthy sample, and reports task-related brain activation (ventral striatum). No exclusion criteria met in abstract.

Excluded because the study does not involve an emotion regulation task as defined (I2 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion criteria not met: I2 (no emotion regulation instruction; study examines price-driven expectations on taste, not deliberate regulation of emotional responses). No exclusion criteria (E1/E2) apply based on the abstract.

Abstract provides insufficient methodological detail to determine whether this is a task-based fMRI study reporting task-related activation during an emotion regulation task. Title suggests neural measures of emotion regulation, but inclusion criteria I1–I4 are not demonstrated in the abstract. Include for full-text review to confirm whether task-based fMRI and task activation results are reported.

Abstract indicates an empirical task-based fMRI study examining emotional reactivity and regulation in generalized anxiety disorder, reporting frontolimbic (prefrontal and amygdala) engagement. This fits I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I3 (clinical human participants), and I4 (task-related brain activation reported). No exclusion criteria are met. Include for full-text review to confirm methods and control group details.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study using effortful affective reappraisal (downregulation of negative affect), includes depressed and nondepressed human groups with separate control comparisons, and reports task-related activation and connectivity results relevant to emotion regulation.

No exclusion criteria met (E1/E2: none). Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion not met / not demonstrated: I2 — the study examines pain processing/meditation during thermal stimulation, not regulation of emotional responses to visual stimuli as specified by the review objective. Therefore excluded for not addressing the review objective.
Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study with human participants that includes an explicit emotion regulation task (reappraisal) and reports brain activation results; no exclusion criteria are met.

Task-based fMRI study of cognitive emotion regulation (positive reappraisal) in human participants; reports task-related activation in ventral striatum, vmPFC, amygdala and connectivity results. No exclusion criteria appear to be met from the abstract.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study in human participants (women) reporting task-related neural activation (satisfies I1, I3, I4). The abstract does not specify that participants performed an explicit emotion-regulation task (I2 not demonstrated). Insufficient information to exclude; include for full-text review to confirm I2.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study (I1) with human participants (I3) and reports task-related activations (I4), but does not describe an emotion regulation instruction or strategy; participants appear to passively process negative vs neutral faces. Therefore I2 (emotion regulation task) is not met. No exclusion criteria are met (E1/E2).

Task-based fMRI using an emotional faces paradigm (viewing emotional stimuli without regulation is allowed by review). Human clinical older adult sample (late-life depression). Reports task-related functional activation. No exclusion criteria met.

No emotion regulation instructions are reported (I2 not met). The study is a task-based fMRI and reports task-related activations (I1, I4 met). It enrolls only VCFS patients without a separately reported control group (I3 not demonstrated). No exclusion criteria clearly apply (none met).

Task-based fMRI with human adolescent participants and task-related brain activation are clearly reported (I1, I3, I4). The abstract does not clearly state that participants were instructed to regulate their emotional responses (I2 uncertain)—it describes inhibitory control in presence of socioaffective cues, which may reflect cognitive control of emotion. Insufficient detail to determine whether this meets the review’s definition of an emotion regulation task, so include for full-text review.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study of human participants performing cognitive emotion regulation (CER) during aversive conditioning and reports task-related ventral striatal and network activation/results. This meets inclusion criteria I1–I4 and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text needed for details and contrasts for meta-analysis, so include for full-text review.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI emotion regulation study (amygdala neurofeedback during aversive-picture viewing) reporting task-related activation and connectivity, but it does not indicate whether a control group is reported for this clinical BPD sample (I3 not demonstrated). Include for full-text review to resolve this uncertainty.

Task-based fMRI study with human participants (24 women) performing cognitive reappraisal/social-distance emotion regulation; reports task-related brain activation (dmPFC, aPCC, amygdala) and peripheral measures. Meets inclusion I1–I4; no exclusion criteria met.

Abstract reports a film-based emotion reactivity and regulation task performed in an MRI scanner, with age-related changes in emotional reactivity and reported brain activation (middle frontal gyrus). Fits task-based fMRI emotion regulation studies; no exclusion criteria met.

Abstract reports a controlled fMRI study in patients with bipolar disorder, indicating human clinical participants with a control group (I3). However, it does not specify whether the fMRI was task-based, whether participants performed an emotion-regulation or visual-stimulus viewing task, or whether task-related activation results are reported (I1, I2, I4 unclear). Include for full-text review to determine task details and reported activations.

This is a task-based fMRI study with human participants instructed to increase or decrease their affective responses to visual images. The abstract reports task-related brain activation results. All inclusion criteria (I1–I4) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Excluded because the abstract does not describe an emotion regulation task (I2 not met). No exclusion criteria apply (E1,E2 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion criteria not met: I2 (no instruction to regulate emotions; participants viewed threatening stimuli and activations were correlated with personality).

Task-based fMRI with implicit and explicit emotional-face tasks; reports task-related activation and connectivity; includes clinical and control groups. Addresses review objective (viewing/regulating emotional visual stimuli). No exclusion criteria met.

Study reports resting-state functional connectivity in bipolar disorder, not a task-based fMRI emotion regulation study. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human clinical participants). Inclusion IDs not met or not demonstrated: I1 (no task-based fMRI), I2 (no emotion regulation task), I4 (no task-related activation reported).

Meets all inclusion criteria: task-based fMRI (I1); uses a cognitive control/'reality checking' emotion regulation strategy during anticipation (I2); healthy human participants (I3); reports task-related brain activation results (I4). No exclusion criteria met; include for full-text review.

EXCLUDED: No evidence participants were instructed to regulate their emotional responses (I2 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human adolescent participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Exclusion criteria met: none (E[]). The study used a social exclusion (Cyberball) paradigm assessing emotional responsivity, not an emotion regulation task.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study in healthy human participants who viewed and regulated emotional pictures, reports BOLD/neuroimaging results comparing regulation vs viewing. Meets I1–I4; no exclusions apply.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study of emotion regulation in human participants (depressed patients) and reports prefrontal activation predicting symptom trajectory over 6 months, satisfying I1-I4; no exclusion criteria are met.

Abstract reports a human trial teaching cognitive reappraisal to alter neural (reward/inhibitory region) responses to high-fat/high-sugar foods, meeting I2 (emotion regulation/cognitive reappraisal) and I3 (human participants). The abstract does not explicitly state task-based fMRI (I1) or clearly report task-related brain activation results (I4), so full-text review is needed to confirm fMRI and activation reporting.

Abstract does not show participants performed an emotion-regulation task (I2). It reports reappraisal of meaning for literary texts but not instruction to regulate emotional responses to stimuli; stimuli are textual rather than clearly emotional visual images. Inclusion criteria met: I1, I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met/demonstrated: I2. No exclusion criteria clearly met.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation) in 54 healthy participants, reporting task-related functional connectivity alterations comparing reappraisal versus maintain. All inclusion criteria I1–I4 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

Task-based fMRI in healthy human participants that manipulates and reduces appetitive/emotional responses to visual food cues via an aversive aftertaste (a regulation-like cognitive control of appetite). Reports task-related brain activation. No exclusion criteria are met.

The study is a task-based fMRI study (I1), with human participants (I3), and reports task-related activations (I4), but it does not involve participants performing an emotion regulation task—it uses an emotional oddball/distraction paradigm without instructions to regulate emotional responses (I2 not met). No exclusion criteria are met (none applicable).

Task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation) in human participants (psychosis-prone vs low), reporting task-related brain activation and functional connectivity. Fits all inclusion criteria; no exclusion criteria apply.

Task-based fMRI study using emotional (angry/neutral) faces during a working-memory task with patient and control groups; reports task-related functional connectivity differences. The review objective allows studies that view emotional stimuli without explicit regulation, so include for full-text to confirm whether regulation instructions were used. Inclusion criteria met: I1, I3, I4. I2 (explicit emotion regulation) not demonstrated in abstract.

Task-based rtfMRI neurofeedback in human participants that involves voluntary self-regulation of emotional (amygdala) activity with positive emotion induction and reports task-related connectivity/activation results; meets inclusion criteria I1–I4. No exclusion criteria met from abstract.

Task-based fMRI with human participants and reported task-related activation, but abstract does not indicate any emotion-regulation instructions. The review accepts studies that view visual stimuli without regulating, so include for full-text review to confirm whether stimuli were passively viewed or regulated.

The abstract describes a task-based (3T fMRI) study using the shifted-attention emotion appraisal task (SEAT), a test of emotional processing and regulation, in human participants given DHEA or placebo, and reports task-related brain activation and connectivity results. No exclusion criteria are met. Recommend full-text review.

Task-based fMRI with adolescent participants and task-related activation reported (I1, I3, I4). Abstract does not clearly state participants were instructed to regulate their emotional responses (I2 not demonstrated). Because it’s unclear whether the task constitutes an emotion-regulation instruction rather than measurement of emotion-related distraction, include for full-text review to determine I2.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study in human patients performing an emotion regulation task (cognitive reappraisal to down-regulate negative affect), and reports task-related brain activation results. This satisfies inclusion criteria I1–I4; no exclusion criteria are met.

Abstract reports task-based fMRI of affective anticipation (I1), human combat veterans sample (I3), and neural convergence/task-related results (I4). It does not specify that participants were instructed to regulate their emotional responses (I2 not demonstrated). No exclusion criteria are met. Include for full-text review to determine whether an explicit emotion-regulation instruction/task was used.

Task-based fMRI study reporting task-related cortical–amygdala coupling during anticipation of a public speech (I1, I4). It examines anticipatory emotional processes relevant to emotion regulation, but the abstract does not state that participants were instructed to regulate nor whether a control group is reported, so full-text review is needed to confirm I2 and I3.

Task-based fMRI in human participants manipulating incentives to regulate emotional reactions to visual/peer stimuli; reports task-related neural activation differences for regulation of positive vs negative emotions. Fits broad definition of emotion regulation (deliberative regulation in decision-making) and meets all inclusion criteria.

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human clinical sample reported). Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I1 (no clear task-based fMRI described), I2 (no emotion-regulation task or instructions described), I4 (no task-related activation results reported). Abstract describes structural, diffusion, and functional connectivity analyses rather than an emotion-regulation or stimulus-viewing task. No exclusion criteria clearly met.

No exclusion criteria met. The study is a resting-state fMRI investigation of euthymic Type I bipolar patients and does not involve a task-based emotion regulation or viewing paradigm, nor report task-related activation. Inclusion met: I3 (human clinical participants). Inclusion not met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related activation).

Task-based fMRI with adolescents and adults performing directed (emotion judgment) and incidental (age judgment) face processing conditions, providing contrasts that reflect cognitive control of emotion versus passive viewing. Reports task-related brain activation results. Fits meta-analysis objective of studies that regulate emotional responses or view them without regulating.

Task-based fMRI study with human clinical and control groups (Complicated Grief, Non-Complicated, Nonbereaved) reporting task-related activations. Abstract does not specify an explicit emotion-regulation instruction (ecStroop likely measures emotional processing/attentional bias rather than directed regulation), so criterion I2 is unclear from abstract alone; full-text needed to confirm whether the paradigm meets the review’s emotion-regulation definition.

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met or not demonstrated: I1 (no mention of task-based fMRI), I2 (not an emotion-regulation task for visual stimuli; focuses on pain modulation), I3 (participants/sample not clearly reported), I4 (no task-related brain activation results reported).

Task-based fMRI study in human children (ages 8–10) performing voluntary emotion regulation (reappraisal/suppression) of sad film excerpts; reports task-related brain activation loci. No exclusion criteria are met.

Task-based fMRI study in humans (patients with SAD) where participants performed emotion regulation (reappraisal) of social evaluation and the paper reports task-related brain activation changes; meets I1-I4 and no exclusion criteria are met based on the abstract.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study investigating emotion regulation in ADHD, matching the review objective. However, it does not specify whether a separate control group was reported or explicitly state task-related activation results in the abstract. Include for full-text review to confirm control group reporting and reported activation results.

Study uses Cyberball to measure neural responses to social exclusion but does not indicate participants were instructed to regulate their emotional responses. Thus it does not meet the emotion-regulation task criterion (I2).

Task-based fMRI study examining neural circuitry supporting emotion regulation using an emotional n-back task in human clinical groups; reports task-related anterior cingulate activation distinguishing bipolar vs unipolar depressed females. Inclusion criteria I1, I3, and I4 are clearly met; I2 is reasonably met because the study targets emotion regulation circuitry and uses emotional stimuli (fits the review objective of regulation or viewing). No exclusion criteria apply.

Study is a task-based fMRI with human participants instructed to maintain or regulate emotional responses to visual social stimuli (regulation task). Reports task-related brain activation analyses. No exclusion criteria met (not a review; not mere perspective-taking).

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human clinical group), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion criterion not met: I2 (no evidence participants performed an emotion regulation task—abstract describes responses/recognition of emotional stimuli rather than instructed regulation), so excluded based on I2 not demonstrated.

Excluded because the task is a simple motor response flexibility task rather than an emotion regulation task. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (adolescent human participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion not met: I2 (does not involve regulation of emotional responses to visual stimuli). No exclusion criteria met (E1,E2).

I2 (emotion regulation task) not demonstrated: abstract describes viewing threatening stimuli and measuring reactivity but no instruction to regulate. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (healthy human participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). No exclusion criteria met (E1,E2).

Task-based fMRI study in 19 healthy adults that explicitly instructs emotion regulation (cognitive reappraisal and expressive suppression) and natural attending; reports task-related brain activation. No exclusion criteria met.

Task-based fMRI study reporting cognitive emotion regulation (reappraisal) during scanning in human participants (female sample) with task-related brain activation results (amygdala and prefrontal coupling). No exclusion criteria met and all inclusion criteria are satisfied.

Abstract reports a tDCS-fMRI study aiming to modulate implicit emotion regulation in human participants but does not clearly state a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation task or report task-related activation. Key inclusion criteria (I1, I2, I4) are uncertain from abstract alone, so INCLUDE for full-text review to clarify.

Study uses resting-state fMRI rather than a task-based emotion regulation or viewing paradigm. It includes clinical (ASD) and control participants (I3 met) but does not involve an emotion regulation task (I2), is not task-based (I1), and does not report task-related activation results (I4). No exclusion criteria (E1/E2) apply.

Excluded (E2): This is a task-based fMRI study (I1) with human participants (I3) reporting task-related activations (I4), but it measures mentalizing/perspective-taking without instruction to alter participants' emotional responses—fits exclusion E2; I2 (emotion-regulation task) not met or demonstrated.

Study is a task-based fMRI with human participants and reports task-related activation (I1, I3, I4 satisfied). However, participants performed a projective storytelling/perspective-taking AAP task without instructions to regulate emotion, meeting exclusion E2. Inclusion I2 (emotion-regulation task) is not demonstrated.

Task-based fMRI investigating emotional conflict and reports fronto-limbic activity/connectivity (meets I1 and I4). Abstract does not clearly state that participants were instructed to regulate their emotional responses per inclusion definition (I2 not demonstrated) and does not specify a separately reported control group (I3 not demonstrated). Because key details are missing but the study likely fits the review, include for full-text review.

Task-based fMRI with human participants viewing religious vs nonreligious images during painful stimulation; contemplation of the religious image led to emotional detachment (an emotion-regulation-like process) and the paper reports task-related brain activations (right VLPFC). Fits inclusion criteria for emotion regulation to visual stimuli and reports brain activation results.

Study uses resting-state fMRI and examines amygdala functional connectivity in PTSD, not a task-based emotion regulation or viewing task and does not report task-related activations. Inclusion met: I3 (human clinical participants). Inclusion not met: I1, I2, I4. No exclusion criteria met.

Study used resting-state fMRI (rs-fMRI) rather than a task-based paradigm. It does not involve an emotion-regulation task with visual stimuli or report task-related activation results. It includes human clinical participants (MDD) but fails I1, I2, and I4. No exclusion criteria are met.

Study uses implicit emotional processing (gender judgment) without instructions to regulate emotion. Exclusion IDs met: []. Inclusion IDs met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human clinical and control groups), I4 (reports task-related task activation/connectivity). Inclusion IDs not met: I2 (participants performing an emotion regulation task).

Study used task-based fMRI during a psychosocial stress task and reports task-related hippocampal activation; satisfies I1, I3, I4. Abstract does not describe an emotion-regulation task (e.g., reappraisal or instructed regulation of emotional responses to visual stimuli), so I2 is not demonstrated. No exclusion criteria are met.

Abstract suggests neural investigation of regulating negative autobiographical memories but does not clearly state task-based fMRI, that participants performed an explicit emotion-regulation task, or that task-related activation results are reported. Insufficient information to confirm inclusion criteria from abstract alone; include for full-text review.

Task-based fMRI in human participants manipulating perceived control over painful stimuli as a form of cognitive reappraisal/emotion regulation; reports task-related brain activation (dACC, alPFC). Fits broad definition of reappraisal/antecedent-focused regulation. No exclusion criteria met.

No evidence participants were instructed to regulate their emotional responses (e.g., reappraisal/acceptance); task is memory retrieval of painful vs non-painful events. Exclusion: none. Inclusions met: I1, I3, I4. Inclusion not met: I2 (emotion regulation task not demonstrated).

Abstract reports task-based fMRI in a normative human sample and multivoxel pattern results predicting affective valence/arousal (I1, I3, I4). It does not state participants performed an emotion regulation task (I2 not demonstrated). Because inclusion is uncertain from abstract alone, include for full-text review.

Task-based fMRI in human participants using distancing (a form of cognitive reappraisal) to downregulate emotional responses to visual social stimuli; reports whole-brain task-related activation results (amygdala, PFC, precuneus, etc.). Meets inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria apparent.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study using a cognitive reappraisal strategy (core emotion-regulation approach) with reported neural activity/connectivity and refers to human participants. It does not specify regulation of emotional responses to visual stimuli explicitly, so inclusion in the visual-stimulus-specific meta-analysis is uncertain — include for full-text review.

Task-based fMRI with human participants performing an implicit emotion-regulation task (derogation of attractive alternatives). Reports task-related brain activation results (VLPFC, pDMPFC, ventral striatum). Meets inclusion criteria I1–I4; no exclusion criteria apparent from abstract.

The study is task-based fMRI with OCD and control groups and reports task-related activation (I1, I3, I4). However, the task elicits shame and guilt via imagined scenarios and does not describe any emotion-regulation instructions (reappraisal, distancing, acceptance) or viewing/regulating of visual stimuli. Inclusion criterion I2 (emotion regulation task) is not demonstrated; no exclusion criteria are met.

Abstract reports an empirical task-based fMRI study in children performing emotion regulation while viewing emotionally expressive faces and reports task-related ACC activation patterns. This meets inclusion criteria I1–I4; no exclusion criteria apply.

Longitudinal task-based fMRI where adults performed effortful emotion regulation of negative stimuli; reports task-related activation (amygdala, ventrolateral/dorsolateral PFC). Meets I1-I4; no exclusion criteria met.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study where participants (SAD patients) used an instructed emotion-regulation strategy (“reality-checking”) during anticipation and perception of emotional stimuli and reports task-related brain activation results. Inclusion criteria I1, I2, and I4 are clearly met. It is unclear from the abstract whether a separate healthy control group is reported (I3 not demonstrated), so include for full-text review to confirm.

Task-based fMRI in human participants reporting task-related activations (amygdala/prefrontal). Abstract describes 'cognitive evaluation' of emotional faces suggestive of regulation but does not clearly state participants were instructed to regulate emotions; include for full-text review to confirm I2.

Meets inclusion: task-based fMRI (I1); uses an emotion regulation task (cognitive reappraisal) (I2); human adolescent participants (I3); reports task-related brain activation (amygdala and prefrontal activation) (I4). No exclusion criteria met. Abstract clearly describes fMRI emotion regulation paradigm with neural results, so include for full-text review.

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human adolescent participants). Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (participants performing an emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation results). The study reports resting-state functional connectivity rather than a task-based emotion regulation paradigm, so it does not meet the meta-analysis inclusion criteria.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study in human (BPD) participants examining neural correlates of provocation-focused rumination, but does not specify that participants regulated emotional responses to visual stimuli or used standard emotion-regulation instructions (e.g., reappraisal). Eligibility for the meta-analysis is therefore uncertain from the abstract and warrants full-text review.

Excluding because the study is a task-based fMRI study with clinical and control adolescent groups and reports task-related activations (I1, I3, I4 met). However, it does not describe an emotion-regulation task or instructions to amplify/dampen emotional responses (I2 not met). No exclusion criteria (E1/E2) apply.

Abstract reports fMRI analysis comparing DAS and NDAS using Granger causality to study emotional networks but does not specify a task-based emotion-regulation or viewing paradigm, nor report task-related activations. Task and regulation details (I1, I2, I4) are not provided, so include for full-text review. I3 (clinical participant group) is satisfied.

Task-based fMRI in human participants (N=24) instructed to view or decrease emotional responses to pictured stimuli (emotion regulation). Reports task-related brain activation. No exclusion criteria met (not a review/meta-analysis, not an empathy/perspective-taking study without regulation instruction).

Abstract reports investigation of behavioral and neural markers of emotion regulation in older adults (human participants), but does not explicitly state it used task-based fMRI, a specific emotion regulation task with visual stimuli, or report task-related activation. Insufficient information to confirm I1, I2, and I4 — include for full-text review.

Task-based rtfMRI neurofeedback study where human participants performed a sustained emotion regulation task (voluntarily modulating positive/negative states) and task-related brain activation results are reported. Meets inclusion criteria I1, I2, I3, I4; no exclusion criteria are apparent from the abstract.

Task-based fMRI study in humans where participants were instructed to up- and down-regulate emotional responses to aversive visual scenes (cognitive reappraisal strategies), and the abstract reports task-related brain activation results (prefrontal, amygdala). No exclusion criteria met.

Task-based fMRI study with human participants viewing emotional visual stimuli (high- and low-arousal pictures) without regulation; reports task-related brain activation results. This directly addresses the review objective of studies that either regulate emotions or view stimuli without regulating. No exclusion criteria met.

Not a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation study: I1 (task-based fMRI) not met, I2 (emotion regulation task) not met, I4 (task-related activations reported) not met. Includes healthy human participants (I3 met). No exclusion criteria (E1,E2) apply.

fMRI task study in adolescents with TBI using an Emotional Go/NoGo paradigm; meets I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human clinical participants), and likely I4 (reports task-related neural results). Abstract does not indicate participants were instructed to regulate their emotions (I2 not demonstrated), so include for full-text review to confirm whether an emotion-regulation or relevant viewing condition is present.

Exclude: Not a task-based fMRI study (I1 not met); uses VBM and resting-state fMRI only, no emotion-regulation task reported (I2 not met); no task-related activation results (I4 not met). Inclusion met: I3 (human participants). No exclusion criteria (E1/E2) clearly met from abstract.

Task-based fMRI with 20 healthy human participants viewing aversive visual stimuli and reporting task-related BOLD activation. Abstract does not describe an instructed emotion-regulation task, but the review objective includes passive viewing of emotional stimuli; thus study is eligible for full-text review.

Study uses resting-state fMRI in MDD psychotherapy rather than a task-based emotion regulation paradigm. Therefore I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), and I4 (task-related activation results) are not met. I3 (human clinical participants) is met. No exclusion criteria (E1/E2) apply.

Exclusion because the study is a task-based fMRI study (I1), includes clinical and control groups (I3), and reports task-related activations (I4), but does not involve participants performing an emotion regulation task or being instructed to regulate (I2 not met). No exclusion criteria were triggered.

Title/abstract indicate a task-based fMRI study in human patients (women with BPD) investigating emotional modulation of response inhibition, but the abstract does not specify whether participants performed an explicit emotion-regulation task or only viewed emotional stimuli, nor does it give task-related activation details. Insufficient information to confirm I2 and I4 from the abstract alone, so include for full-text review.

Task-based fMRI with 21 healthy human participants performing emotion regulation strategies (mindfulness and suppression) in response to emotional visual stimuli; reports task-related brain activation results (amygdala attenuation and connectivity). Satisfies all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are met.

Task-based fMRI in depressed patients performing intentional emotion-introspection to down-regulate unpleasant affect, with task-related brain activation reported (amygdala, insula, PFC). Unclear from abstract whether regulation was applied to visual stimuli, so include for full-text review to resolve this.

Meets all inclusion criteria: task-based fMRI; participants performed effortful emotion regulation (emotional faces n-back assessing voluntary attentional control); includes schizophrenia patients with matched healthy controls reported separately; reports task-related brain activation results. No exclusion criteria are evident from the abstract.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study (I1) where participants explicitly regulate emotion (reduce negative, enhance positive) reflecting CBT-like reappraisal strategies (I2), includes human clinical (medication-free MDD) and matched control groups reported separately (I3), and reports task-related brain activation results (I4). No exclusion criteria are met.

Abstract reports task-based fMRI with human participants and reports task-related brain activation (I1, I3, I4). However, there is no evidence participants performed an emotion regulation task or were instructed to regulate their emotional responses (I2 not demonstrated). No exclusion criteria are met.

Abstract reports task-based fMRI in clinical out-patients examining brain activation to emotional facial expressions (meets I1, I3, I4). It does not state whether participants were instructed to regulate their emotional responses (I2 not demonstrated). No exclusion criteria met. Abstract insufficient to determine regulation vs passive viewing; include for full-text review.

E2 met: this is an empathy/perspective-taking viewing task without instruction to regulate emotions. Inclusion met: I1, I3, I4 (task-based fMRI; human participants; reports task-related activations). Inclusion not met/not demonstrated: I2 (no evidence participants performed an emotion regulation task).

No exclusion criteria met (none). Inclusion criteria met: I1, I2, I3, I4. Inclusion criterion not demonstrated: regulation of emotional responses to visual stimuli as required by the meta-analysis objective — the study used idiographic sadness/guilt induction (autobiographical recall), not visual stimuli. Therefore excluded.

Abstract reports connectivity and treatment-response in major depression but does not describe a task-based emotion-regulation fMRI paradigm or task-related activation. Exclusion criteria: none met. Inclusion met: I3 (clinical participants). Inclusion not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation).

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study in humans (N=20) with task-related brain activation and healthy participants. It is unclear whether participants were instructed to regulate emotions (vs. passive viewing); therefore inclusion for full-text review is warranted to determine if the task meets the review's emotion-regulation criteria.

No explicit emotion-regulation instructions or strategy are described; the study examines anticipatory neural activity during speech anticipation but not a regulation task. Inclusion criteria met: I1, I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met/demonstrated: I2. Exclusion criteria met: none (E1/E2 not applicable).

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human clinical and control adolescent groups), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I2 (no evidence participants performed an emotion regulation task or were instructed to regulate emotional responses; the task was a working-memory paradigm with emotional distracters rather than an explicit regulation instruction).

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study in human participants performing an emotion regulation task (veterans with PTSD and controls), and reports task-related brain activation results (PFC, SMA changes). No exclusion criteria are met. Include for full-text review to extract detailed task contrasts and results.

Included for full-text review. Abstract reports a human (women with PTSD) neuroimaging study of emotional processing, but it does not specify whether a task-based emotion-regulation paradigm was used, whether task-related activation results are reported, or whether a control group is included. I1, I2, and I4 are not demonstrated in the abstract. No exclusion criteria are met based on the abstract.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion met: I3 (human clinical sample: youth with ADHD). Not met: I1 (not task-based; study examines intrinsic functional connectivity/resting-state), I2 (no emotion-regulation task reported), I4 (no task-related activation results reported). Therefore excluded from task-based emotion-regulation fMRI meta-analysis.

Excluded: PET meta-analysis of REM sleep, not a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation study. Inclusion met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion not met: I1 (not task-based fMRI), I2 (not an emotion regulation task), I4 (no task-related activation results reported). No exclusion criteria met.

EXCLUDED because the study investigates neural substrates of visual exploration/saccades, not emotion regulation. Exclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion criteria not met: I2 (no emotion regulation task or instructions to amplify/dampen emotional responses).

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study using a cognitive reappraisal emotion regulation task in human participants and presents task-related brain activation results (vmPFC tracking of subjective and normative valence). No exclusion criteria are met.

Task-based fMRI in healthy adult humans reporting task-related brain activation (ACC). The abstract does not specify that participants were instructed to perform an emotion regulation strategy (uncertain whether anticipation counts as regulation), so I2 is not demonstrated from abstract alone; include for full-text review to resolve.

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I4 (reports task-related activation). Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I2 (emotion regulation task) — the study uses an interoceptive breathing-load task and mindfulness training without instructed regulation of emotional responses to visual stimuli, so it does not address the review objective.

No exclusion criteria met. The study is a task-based fMRI study (I1), uses human participants (I3), and reports task-related brain activation results (I4). However participants viewed emotional scenes after a depletion manipulation and were not instructed to regulate their emotional responses; thus I2 (an emotion regulation task) is not demonstrated. Therefore exclude based on failure to meet I2.

Task-based fMRI study where participants regulated their own or another person's emotions (interpersonal emotion regulation). Healthy human sample (n=20) and report task-related brain activations. Does not meet exclusion criteria (not merely perspective-taking without regulation).

No exclusion criteria are met. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion criteria not met/demonstrated: I2 (emotion regulation task) — abstract describes neural responses to negative facial stimuli but does not indicate participants were instructed to regulate their emotional responses, so it does not meet the emotion-regulation requirement.

E2 met: empathy study assessing spontaneous perception of others' pain without instructions to amplify/dampen emotional responses. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human ASD and control groups), I4 (task-related brain activations reported). Inclusion not met: I2 (no evidence of an emotion-regulation instruction/task).

Abstract reports a task-based whole-brain fMRI study with 55 healthy human participants performing instructed regulation of negative emotion (and viewing without regulating). Task-related activation results are reported (GLM contrasts and task-rest interactions). No exclusion criteria are met.

Task-based fMRI study using an affective face-processing task (likely passive viewing), with social anxiety disorder participants; reports task-related activation (left amygdala) and functional connectivity changes pre/post iCBT. The review accepts both emotion regulation and passive viewing paradigms, so inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is a task-based fMRI experiment in healthy humans reporting task-related brain activations (I1, I3, I4 met). However, participants voluntarily regulated heart rate (physiological arousal) rather than regulating an emotional response to visual stimuli; the task does not meet the review's emotion-regulation-with-visual-stimuli criterion (I2 not demonstrated). No exclusion criteria are met.

Abstract reports task-based fMRI in human 4–6-year-old children examining functional brain activity related to emotion regulation. It is unclear whether participants were instructed to explicitly regulate emotions, so include for full-text review to confirm I2.

Excluded because abstract does not describe an emotion regulation task (I2 not met): the study examines decision-induced rationalization without instructions to regulate emotional responses. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), I4 (reports task-related activations). No exclusion criteria met.

Task-based rtfMRI neurofeedback study in human combat veterans performing emotion regulation (positive autobiographical recall); reports task-related brain activation mediators and includes experimental and control groups. No exclusion criteria met.

Abstract does not specify a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation paradigm or report task-related brain activation results, but studies adults (human participants). Insufficient information to determine inclusion, so include for full-text review.

EXCLUDED because inclusion criterion I2 (emotion regulation task) is not met: study uses a Go/No-Go punishment/impulsivity paradigm, not an instructed emotion-regulation (e.g., reappraisal) task. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human healthy participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). No exclusion criteria (E1,E2) apply.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI RCT where patients viewed negative images or intentionally down-regulated affect using taught strategies, reports symptom change and normalization of brain activation—meeting all inclusion criteria and no exclusions evident.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (human clinical sample with control group). Inclusion criteria not met: I1 (study is resting-state, not task-based fMRI), I2 (no emotion regulation task performed), I4 (no task-related activation reported). Therefore excluded based on failure to meet task-based/emotion-regulation inclusion criteria.

EXCLUDE: Study uses structural MRI (voxel-based morphometry) and behavioral correlations, not task-based fMRI, and does not report task-related brain activation. Inclusion met: I2 (emotion reappraisal task), I3 (healthy and patient groups reported). Inclusion not met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I4 (task-related brain activation). No exclusion criteria met.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study using an emotional Stroop (eStroop) task assessing affective control (meets I1 and I2). Human clinical sample with 50 LLD and remaining participants serving as controls (meets I3). Task-related neural activation results are reported (MFG/MEG activity) (meets I4). No exclusion criteria are met.

Task-based fMRI study where participants with GAD performed explicit emotion regulation (acceptance, worry, suppression) and the abstract reports task-related brain activations and connectivity. Inclusion criteria met: I1, I2, I4. The abstract does not state whether a separate control group was included, so I3 is not demonstrated. No exclusion criteria met. Recommend full-text review to confirm sample/comparison details.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (healthy human participants), I4 (reports task-related connectivity/activation). Inclusion not met: I2 — study examines passive processing of emotional faces and genetic effects, not an emotion regulation instruction/strategy.

E2 met: study uses Theory-of-Mind/perspective-taking processing without instruction to amplify or dampen emotion. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human clinical and control groups). Inclusion not met/not demonstrated: I2 (no emotion-regulation task), I4 (reports connectivity rather than explicit task-related activation results).

Abstract reports task-based fMRI in human adolescents during an emotion regulation task (including passive viewing of negative vs neutral visual stimuli) and reports task-related vmPFC–amygdala functional connectivity linked to psychopathology, matching the review objective and inclusion criteria.

Task-based fMRI where participants ignored task-irrelevant unpleasant words (emotional interference), representing cognitive control of emotion/emotion regulation; includes non-patient groups (high AP/AR/AD and controls) and reports task-related functional connectivity results. All inclusion criteria I1–I4 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

Abstract describes task-based fMRI with human participants and task-related activations, but does not involve an emotion-regulation instruction or strategy (e.g., reappraisal/acceptance) nor explicit regulation of emotional responses to visual stimuli; therefore I2 not met. No exclusion criteria clearly apply.

E2: Study examines perception/evaluation of others (active listening) without instructions to amplify or dampen participants' own emotional responses (no emotion-regulation instruction). Inclusion met: I1, I3, I4. Inclusion not met: I2 (no evidence of an emotion-regulation task such as reappraisal or instructed modulation).

Task-based fMRI in adolescents/young adults reporting rVLPFC activation to negative emotional words and links to emotion reappraisal and alcohol use. The abstract does not clearly state whether participants were instructed to regulate emotion (versus passive viewing), so include for full-text review to confirm I2.

No evidence participants performed an emotion-regulation task (I2 not met). Abstract describes passive viewing and rating of aversive/neutral scenes; reports task fMRI activations (I1, I4) in clinical and control groups (I3). No exclusion criteria met.

Excluded because the study does not involve an emotion regulation task (I2 not met). It is a task-based fMRI study with healthy human participants and reports task-related activation (I1, I3, I4 met). No exclusion criteria apply.

Exclusion: none of the exclusion criteria apply. Inclusion met: I3 (human clinical sample with separate controls). Inclusion NOT met: I1 (not task-based; resting-state fMRI), I2 (no emotion-regulation task), I4 (no task-related activation results reported). Therefore exclude.

Task-based fMRI in healthy humans; reports task-related activations. The emotional oddball requires distinguishing targets while ignoring negative vs neutral distractors, which involves cognitive control of emotional distraction (fits broad emotion-regulation or view-only inclusion). No exclusion criteria met.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study where human participants used cognitive reappraisal to regulate cravings (personal-food images), and reports task-related neural activation (frontoparietal network, multivariate analyses). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a resting-state fMRI study of emotional intelligence, not a task-based emotion regulation study. Inclusion met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion not met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related activation results). No exclusion criteria met (E1,E2 not applicable).

E2 met: study examined empathy for others' pain (participants observed needles inserted into body parts) without any instruction to amplify or dampen their emotional response; thus it is not an emotion regulation task. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), I4 (reports task-related activation). Inclusion not met: I2 (no evidence of an instructed emotion regulation task).

Abstract does not report whether this is a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation study or whether task-related activation contrasts meet inclusion criteria. Title suggests affect processing in methamphetamine dependence but provides insufficient detail. Include for full-text review to determine I1, I2, and I4.

Abstract reports human participants with social anxiety and neural/behavioral responses but does not specify that tasks were fMRI-based or involved explicit emotion regulation (or pure viewing), nor does it state task-related brain activation results. Key eligibility (I1, I2, I4) cannot be confirmed from abstract alone, so include for full-text review.

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human clinical and healthy control groups), I4 (task-related connectivity results).
