It studies a clinical sample (emotional distress disorders) but does not state whether a separate control group is reported, so I3 is not clearly demonstrated. No exclusion criteria are met. Include for full-text review to verify presence of a control group and full task details.

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI not stated in abstract), I2 (classical conditioning/nocebo paradigm is not an explicit emotion-regulation task), I4 (no report of task-related brain activation results in abstract). I3 (human participants) is not explicitly stated. Abstract lacks evidence of the required emotion-regulation fMRI paradigm, so exclude.

Task-based fMRI in human adolescent participants reporting task-related brain activation. The abstract does not clearly state an emotion-regulation instruction (only responses to social feedback/anticipation), so eligibility for a regulation-focused meta-analysis is uncertain; include for full-text review to determine whether it fits regulation/viewing criteria.

Study uses resting-state fMRI (tonic connectivity) rather than a task-based emotion-regulation paradigm. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human clinical participants). Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation results).

No evidence participants were instructed to regulate their emotional responses (I2 not demonstrated). Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human clinical and control groups), I4 (reports task-related activation). Exclusion criteria met: none ([]). Therefore EXCLUDED due to missing I2.

E2 met: participants judged another's affect (perspective-taking/empathy) with no instruction to amplify/dampen their own emotions. Inclusion: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human older adult sample), I4 (reports task-related brain activation) are satisfied. Inclusion I2 is not demonstrated (no emotion-regulation instructions reported).

Abstract is truncated and provides insufficient information to determine whether participants performed an emotion-regulation task (I2). Title indicates a human task-based fMRI fear-conditioning study reporting BOLD results in vmPFC, satisfying I1, I3, and I4. No exclusion criteria are met. Include for full-text review to assess whether emotion regulation instructions were used.

Abstract reports neuroimaging (amygdala) measures tied to regulation, describes emotion- and pain-regulation paradigms in human participants, and reports task-related brain activation linked to regulation success. This satisfies inclusion criteria I1–I4 and no exclusion criteria are indicated.

No task-based emotion-regulation fMRI reported. Study is structural and functional connectivity (likely resting-state) in MDD with/without suicide attempts. Inclusion met: I3. Inclusion not met/not demonstrated: I1, I2, I4. No exclusion criteria met (E[]).

Excluded because inclusion criterion I2 (emotion regulation task) is not met: the study examined neural responses to narrative texts and individual appraisal styles without instructions to regulate emotional responses; stimuli are textual narratives rather than visual regulation tasks. Inclusion criteria met: I1, I3, I4. Exclusion criteria met: none (E1/E2 not applicable).

Abstract lacks sufficient detail to confirm I1 (task-based fMRI) and I2 (participants instructed to regulate emotion) or whether visual emotional stimuli were merely viewed; title suggests negative emotional distraction but task details and presence of control group are not reported. No exclusion criteria are met. Include for full-text review to determine eligibility.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study in a clinical group (IED) probing amygdala–OFC reactivity to social threat and reports neural findings, so I1, I3, and I4 are met. It is unclear whether an explicit emotion-regulation instruction was used (I2 not demonstrated). No exclusion criteria met; include for full-text review to determine I2.

Excluded because this is a resting-state fMRI study, not a task-based emotion regulation or viewing task. Inclusion met: I3 (clinical and control groups reported). Inclusion not met: I1 (not task-based fMRI), I2 (no emotion regulation task), I4 (no task-related brain activation reported). Exclusion criteria met: none (E1,E2 not applicable).

Task-based fMRI in human participants with alcohol use disorder examining cognitive regulation of craving and negative emotion, reporting PFC recruitment and neural mechanisms (task-related brain activation). Meets I1, I2, I3, I4; no exclusion criteria apparent.

Task-based emotional go/no-go study reporting neural overactivation (fronto-striatal), i.e., task fMRI with emotional visual stimuli and clinical group (euthymic bipolar) and reported task-related brain activation. Fits meta-analysis inclusion (regulation/cognitive control or viewing of emotional stimuli). No exclusion criteria met.

Study is a task-based fMRI in humans reporting task-related activation (I1, I3, I4). However it examines reward processing using a monetary incentive delay task without any indication of an emotion-regulation instruction or strategy, so I2 (emotion regulation task) is not met. No exclusion criteria met.

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion IDs not met or not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI not demonstrated — study reports structural MRI and resting-state fMRI), I2 (not an emotion-regulation task — Go/No-Go measures response inhibition, not regulation of emotional responses), I4 (no task-related brain activation results reported). Therefore exclude from this emotion-regulation task-based fMRI meta-analysis.

Meets all inclusion criteria: task-based fMRI with an emotion regulation paradigm (I1, I2), healthy human participants (I3), and reports task-related functional activity during emotion reactivity/regulation (I4). No exclusion criteria met. Include for full-text review.

Task-based fMRI with human participants viewing and rating emotional pictures and reporting task-related brain activation (I1, I3, I4). However, emotion regulation was not explicitly instructed—study examines spontaneous regulation, so I2 (emotion regulation task) is uncertain from the abstract. No exclusion criteria are met. Include for full-text review to determine whether spontaneous regulation meets I2.

EXCLUDED: study used resting-state fMRI, not a task-based emotion regulation paradigm. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (human participants; MDD patients and controls reported separately). Inclusion criteria not met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). No exclusion criteria (E1/E2) applied.

Abstract reports an fMRI study in adolescents with bipolar depression examining neurofunctional effects related to emotional regulation, but does not specify that participants performed an emotion-regulation task or that task-related activation results are reported. Insufficient information to confirm I1, I2, and I4, so include for full-text review.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study using a well-validated emotion regulation task in human participants (drug-naïve IGD youth and matched controls) and presents task-related brain activation results, satisfying inclusion criteria I1–I4. No exclusion criteria are met.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met/demonstrated: I1 (not a task-based fMRI study), I2 (not an emotion-regulation task; study is structural VBM of trauma exposure), I4 (does not report task-related brain activation). Study used structural MRI/voxel-based morphometry, so EXCLUDED.

Abstract reports an fMRI study of implicit processing of negative emotions in motor conversion disorder patients, indicating a task-based human neuroimaging study with a clinical group. However the abstract does not specify whether participants explicitly regulated emotions or merely viewed stimuli (I2 unclear) nor does it state task-related activation results (I4 unclear). Include for full-text review to determine if it meets I2 and I4.

Abstract reports fMRI connectivity findings in bipolar I disorder (human clinical sample) but does not describe a task-based emotion-regulation or viewing paradigm or report task-related activations. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human clinical participants). Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation).

Excluded because E2 applies: this is an empathy/perspective-taking task (MET) with no evidence participants were instructed to amplify or dampen their emotional responses. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human clinical + control groups), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion not met: I2 (no demonstrated emotion regulation instructions).

Study reports neural activity to partner facial expressions predicting self-regulation after conflict in human participants, indicating task-related brain activation; however the abstract does not clearly state fMRI or explicit regulation instructions, so include for full-text review.

Abstract reports adolescent human participants and associations of OFC connectivity with mood/anxiety in marijuana users, but does not specify a task-based emotion-regulation fMRI paradigm or report task-related activation. Insufficient information to determine I1, I2, and I4, so include for full-text review to verify task and activation details.

Study used task-based fMRI evaluating perceived healthiness of foods, but participants were not instructed to regulate their emotional responses (no reappraisal/acceptance/distancing etc.). Inclusion met: I1, I3, I4. Inclusion not met: I2 (no evidence of emotion regulation instruction). No exclusion criteria met.

Task-based fMRI with gambling and sad videotape viewing, includes clinical (PG) and healthy control groups, and reports task-related brain activation. The abstract does not specify an emotion-regulation instruction (only viewing), so inclusion criterion I2 is not clearly satisfied; full text needed to determine if passive viewing meets review scope or if regulation instructions were given.

Excluded because the abstract does not indicate an emotion-regulation instruction (I2 not demonstrated): participants viewed aversive vs neutral images during fMRI without evidence of regulation. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human clinical and control groups), I4 (reports task-related activation). Inclusion criteria not met: I2 (emotion regulation task). Exclusion criteria met: none (E1, E2 not applicable).

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study of emotion downregulation (frontal-amygdala connectivity) in euthymic bipolar I patients and healthy controls and reports task-related frontal and limbic activation/connectivity results. This satisfies I1–I4 and no exclusion criteria apply.

Study used resting-state fMRI pre/post mindfulness in healthy volunteers with no task-based fMRI or emotion-regulation task and reports resting-state connectivity (not task activations). Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion-regulation task), I4 (task-related activation results).

Task-based fMRI in human clinical and control groups reporting task-related ACC activations during an emotionally salient cue-reactivity task. The abstract does not state explicit emotion-regulation instructions, but the meta-analysis objective allows viewing without regulating; full text needed to confirm whether an explicit regulation contrast exists. Include for full-text review.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (human participants: BD and genetic high-risk). Inclusion criteria not met: I1 (not task-based fMRI; resting-state), I2 (no emotion-regulation task), I4 (no task-related activation reported).

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human participants: postmortem human brain and living healthy subjects). Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI not reported), I2 (no emotion regulation task; study focuses on noncoding RNA and behavioral/aggressive phenotypes, not regulation of emotional responses to visual stimuli), I4 (no task-related brain activation results reported). Therefore exclude based on failure to meet required inclusion criteria.

Task-based fMRI study (I1) with children and adults viewing emotional video clips and reporting task-related brain activation results (I4). Participant sample qualifies (I3). The abstract does not state an explicit emotion-regulation instruction (I2 not demonstrated), but the review objective allows passive viewing; include for full-text review to confirm applicability.

Study examines neural processing of a conditioned threat cue in alcohol-dependent men (human clinical sample) using a task-based paradigm involving anticipation/cue exposure. The abstract does not explicitly state fMRI, nor whether participants regulated emotions or simply viewed/anticipated the stressor, and does not clearly report task-related activation; include for full-text to confirm I1, I2, and I4.

Human fMRI connectivity study targeting cortico-limbic circuitry under acute tryptophan depletion; likely probes emotion-related neural circuits but abstract does not specify a task-based emotion-regulation paradigm or report task-related activations. Insufficient information to confirm I1, I2, I4 — include for full-text review.

Task-based fMRI study reporting neural activation to emotional (anxiety-inducing) visual distractors during a working memory task. Abstract does not state explicit emotion-regulation instructions or whether a control group is reported, so inclusion re: I2 and I3 is uncertain; include for full-text review.

Abstract describes passive emotion perception (viewing multisensory dynamic emotional stimuli) rather than an emotion regulation task; therefore inclusion criterion I2 is not met. It is a task-based fMRI study with healthy participants and reports task-related brain activation (I1, I3, I4 met). No exclusion criteria clearly apply.

Abstract is too brief to confirm key inclusion criteria: it does not explicitly state task-based fMRI, that participants performed an emotion regulation task (versus passive emotion processing), or that task-related activations are reported. Title suggests facial emotion processing in pediatric bipolar disorder, so the study is relevant, but information is insufficient—include for full-text review.

Abstract does not explicitly state that task-based fMRI was used, that participants performed an emotion regulation task (e.g., reappraisal), or that task-related brain activation results are reported. It investigates neural correlates of emotion-attention regulation in schizophrenia, so it may meet inclusion criteria, but the abstract lacks necessary methodological details — include for full-text review to confirm I1, I2, and I4.

Excluded: Study does not involve emotion regulation or viewing emotional stimuli; it investigates motor planning and control. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), I4 (reports task-related activations). Inclusion not met: I2 (emotion regulation task) is not demonstrated. No exclusion criteria met.

Abstract describes passive processing of emotional words in a task-based fMRI study with healthy participants and reports task-related activation and connectivity. However, it does not report an instructed emotion-regulation task (only mentions possible 'unintentional' regulation). Therefore I2 (emotion regulation task) is not demonstrated. No exclusion criteria are met.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study in humans using a social-emotional paradigm requiring control over automatic approach/avoidance actions (emotion regulation), reports task-related aPFC-amygdala activation in healthy police recruits; no exclusion criteria met.

Abstract does not report whether task-based fMRI or an emotion regulation task was used; it describes machine-learning on multimodal neuroimaging in PTSD (human clinical sample). I3 appears met, but I1, I2, and I4 are not demonstrated in the abstract. Include for full-text review to determine task nature and task-related activation reporting.

Abstract reports task-based fMRI cue-exposure in alcohol-dependent humans examining brain activation to alcohol-related cues (fits task-based and cue viewing without regulation). It investigates task-related activation and intervention effects. The abstract does not report a separate control group for the patient sample, so inclusion on that point is uncertain; full-text needed.

Abstract does not specify use of task-based fMRI or report task-related brain activation; it examines frontal control over social-emotional actions predicting HPA-axis stress responsivity in humans, which could reflect an emotion-regulation-related task but is unclear. Insufficient information to confirm I1 and I4; include for full-text review to determine eligibility.

Task-based fMRI in human participants with MDD reporting task-related (effective connectivity) results during happy and fear face processing. Abstract does not state participants were instructed to regulate their emotional responses, so I2 (emotion regulation task) is not confirmed; therefore include for full-text review to determine eligibility.

Abstract reports human older adult clinical and control groups with neuroimaging of PFC activity/connectivity (meets I3). However, it does not specify a task-based fMRI paradigm, nor that participants performed an emotion-regulation task or that task-related activation results are reported (I1, I2, I4 not demonstrated). Insufficient information to determine inclusion—include for full-text review.

Meets I1 (task-based fMRI with stimuli), I3 (human clinical/healthy participants) and I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Does NOT demonstrate I2: no evidence participants performed an emotion-regulation task or were instructed to up-/down-regulate emotion. No exclusion criteria clearly met (exclusion IDs: none). Exclude based on missing I2.

Task-based fMRI in humans viewing masked emotional (happy/fearful) faces; reports task-related activation differences in anterior cingulate and amygdala. Although participants passively viewed stimuli (no regulation instruction), the review includes studies that view emotional stimuli without regulating. Thus the abstract meets the review objective and reports task-related activation results, supporting inclusion for full-text review.

Excluded (E2): study examines empathy for others' pain without instructions to amplify or dampen participants' emotional responses. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), I4 (task-related activation results). Inclusion not met/demonstrated: I2 (no explicit emotion-regulation instruction such as reappraisal/perspective-taking to alter affect).

Task-based fMRI with healthy adults and task-related activation reported, but participants were not instructed to perform an emotion regulation task; the study measured trait emotional suppression (self-report) and passive/automatic responses to masked faces. Inclusion I2 (emotion regulation task) is not met.

No evidence in abstract of task-based fMRI or an emotion-regulation task, and no task-related brain activation results reported. Inclusion met: I3 (clinical geriatric sample). Inclusion not met/demonstrated: I1, I2, I4. Exclusion criteria met: none.

Excluded because this is a structural MRI study of cortical thickness in older adults, not a task-based fMRI study of emotion regulation. Inclusion I3 (human participants) is met. Inclusion I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), and I4 (task-related brain activation results) are not met. No exclusion criteria (E1,E2) apply based on the abstract.

Task-based fMRI with SZ and matched controls; reports task-related brain activation (left IFG) during emotional distractors and WM load. Abstract does not clearly state whether participants were explicitly instructed to regulate emotions (regulation vs. passive ignoring of distractors is ambiguous). Include for full-text review to determine whether I2 (emotion regulation task) is met.

Abstract reports task-based fMRI in human participants and task-related brain activation during emotional discrimination, but it is unclear whether participants were explicitly instructed to regulate their emotional responses (reappraisal/other regulation) versus passive viewing/discrimination. Because I2 (emotion regulation task) is not clearly demonstrated, include for full-text review to confirm eligibility.

Abstract examines neural correlates of emotion regulation in late-life GAD (human clinical sample). However, it does not specify use of a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation paradigm nor clearly report task-related activation in the abstract. Insufficient information to confirm I1 and I4, so include for full-text review.

Task-based fMRI study using real-time neurofeedback for voluntary amygdala down-regulation while viewing aversive pictures in healthy participants; reports task-related connectivity/activation results. Meets I1-I4 and no exclusion criteria apply.

Task-based fMRI study examining acceptance as an emotion-regulation strategy in individuals with BPD; reports neural correlates (brain activation). Fits inclusion criteria I1–I4 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This study is a task-based fMRI fear-conditioning connectivity study in human participants that reports task-related activations (meets I1, I3, I4). However, the abstract does not describe an emotion-regulation task or instructions (no reappraisal/acceptance/distancing or other regulation strategies), so I2 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E1/E2) apply.

Abstract reports an fMRI study of emotion processing/regulation in youth comparing bipolar subtypes and healthy controls, but does not specify whether participants performed an explicit emotion-regulation task (e.g., reappraisal) or details of stimuli. Insufficient information to confirm I2, so include for full-text review.

Abstract does not specify a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation paradigm and appears to examine baseline 'intrinsic' neural circuitry (likely resting-state) in BD patients undergoing CBT. Only inclusion I3 (clinical human sample) is clearly met. I1, I2, and I4 are not demonstrated. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text required to confirm whether task-based emotion-regulation fMRI data are reported.

Study uses voxel-based morphometry (structural MRI) in healthy participants and reports grey matter volume correlations, not a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation experiment. Exclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria met: I3. Inclusion criteria not met: I1, I2, I4.

Exclusion E2: study appears to be an empathy/perspective-taking paradigm (viewing mother-child videos) without instructions to amplify or dampen participants' own emotional responses. Inclusion criteria met: I1, I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met / not demonstrated: I2 (no emotion-regulation task described).

Study used structural MRI (grey matter volume ROI analysis) and did not involve task-based fMRI, an emotion regulation task, or report task-related activation. Inclusion met: I3 (human participants with control groups). Inclusion not met/demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation results). No exclusion criteria were met.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion criterion I2 (participants performing an emotion-regulation task) is not met — the study examines automatic affective modulation by olfactory/auditory stimuli rather than instructed regulation. Also stimuli are olfactory/auditory, not visual as required by the meta-analysis objective. Therefore excluded.

Task-based fMRI with trauma-related and neutral visual stimuli; reports task-related activation correlated with later PTSD severity. Although no emotion-regulation instruction is described, the meta-analysis includes studies that view stimuli without regulating, so the design is relevant. Abstract provides insufficient detail about regulation instructions (if any) and control groups, so include for full-text review.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study of attention network dysfunction in bulimia nervosa, not an emotion-regulation task. Inclusion I1, I3, and I4 appear met; I2 (emotion regulation task/viewing emotional stimuli with/without regulation) is not demonstrated. No exclusion criteria from E1–E2 apply.

This is a structural VBM MRI study comparing loving-kindness meditators and novices; no task-based fMRI, no emotion-regulation task, and no task-related activation results are reported. No exclusion criteria are met. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion criteria not met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion-regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation).

Study used task-based fMRI with human participants and reports task-related activations (I1, I3, I4). However, the task involved valence ratings without any instruction to regulate emotions, so an emotion regulation task is not demonstrated (I2 not met). No exclusion criteria are met.

The study reports fMRI task activations but does not involve an explicit emotion-regulation task as defined (participants play the Ultimatum Game without instructions to amplify/dampen emotions or regulate responses to visual emotional stimuli). Met: I1, I3, I4. Not met: I2. No exclusion criteria (E1/E2) apply.

Abstract reports an fMRI pilot study of mindfulness treatment in cigarette smokers examining reward-related frontostriatal processes but does not specify an emotion-regulation task or whether participants regulated emotional responses to visual stimuli. No exclusion criteria are met. Key information (presence of an emotion-regulation task and task-related activation for regulation vs. view) is missing, so include for full-text review.

Study examines emotion recognition (viewing/perception) in MDD rather than an emotion regulation task. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based functional imaging) and I4 (reports task-related functional alterations). Inclusion not met/not demonstrated: I2 (no evidence participants were instructed to regulate/dampen/amplify emotional responses), I3 (patient/control group reporting not clearly stated). No exclusion criteria met.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study where participants viewed emotional pictures and were instructed to decrease, increase, or not modulate their emotional responses. Human adult participants are implied, and the paper reports task-related brain activation differences after training. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a structural VBM study of gray matter in MDD, not a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation study. Exclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met or not demonstrated: I1 (not task-based fMRI), I2 (no emotion-regulation task), I4 (no task-related activation results), I3 (clinical/control group not demonstrated in abstract).

No emotion regulation task reported (I2 not met). The study is a task-based fMRI pain stimulation study with patient and control groups and reports task-related activations. Exclusion criteria not met.

Task-based BOLD fMRI in healthy adults randomized to compassion vs reappraisal training; participants engaged in instructed emotion-regulation strategies while viewing suffering/non-suffering images; reports task-related neural activation (amygdala, insula, OFC). No exclusion criteria met.

No exclusion criteria met. Study is a structural MRI (voxel-based morphometry) comparison of grey matter volumes in ADHD vs controls, not a task-based fMRI emotion regulation study. Inclusion met: I3 (human clinical participant group). Inclusion NOT met/demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation results).

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study using an emotion regulation strategy to regulate conditioned fear in human participants and reports task-related neural activation results. This meets I1, I2, I3, and I4. No exclusion criteria are met. Include for full-text review.

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion IDs not met: I2 (emotion regulation task) — abstract describes working-memory/circadian wake-promotion, not emotion regulation. Therefore exclude from this review.

Study examines intrinsic brain activity/connectivity (resting-state) in obesity, not a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation study. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion IDs not met/demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation results).

No task-based emotion-regulation paradigm reported. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (human clinical participants). Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation results). No exclusion criteria met (E1,E2).

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I1 (task-based event-related fMRI), I3 (healthy human participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion criteria not met/demonstrated: I2 (this study manipulated attention to emotional stimuli via rTMS and cueing but did not instruct participants to regulate their emotional responses).

Abstract does not report whether the fMRI used a task involving regulation or passive viewing of emotional visual stimuli, nor whether a separate control group and task-related activation results are reported. No exclusion criteria are met based on the abstract. Include for full-text review to determine I1–I4.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study in ASD with intranasal oxytocin, but does not report participants performing an emotion regulation task or being instructed to up-/down-regulate emotional responses. Inclusion I1, I3, I4 are met; I2 is not demonstrated. No exclusion criteria clearly met from abstract.

Exclusion: This is a structural MRI study of gray matter volume in healthy bipolar offspring, not a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation study. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion IDs not met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related activation results).

E2 applies — this is an empathy/perspective-taking fMRI study where participants viewed others' pain without being instructed to regulate (amplify/dampen) their emotional responses. Inclusion I1, I3, I4 are met; I2 is not met/not demonstrated (no emotion-regulation task reported).

Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), I4 (reports task-related activations). Inclusion criterion not met: I2 (no emotion-regulation task; monetary Go/No-go examines inhibition/error processing and punishment anticipation, not instructed regulation of emotional responses to visual stimuli). Exclusion criteria met: None.

Task-based event-related fMRI in healthy humans using an emotional go/no-go (attentional disengagement/cognitive control) task; reports task-related activation (DLPFC) linked to brooding. The task assesses cognitive control of emotional responses (disengagement), fitting the review’s broad definition of emotion regulation.

Exclusion based on lack of an emotion regulation task: I2 not met. This is a task-based fMRI study (I1), includes clinical and control human groups (I3), and reports task-related brain activation results (I4). No exclusion criteria are met (E1,E2 not applicable). The task involved matching emotional faces, not instructions to regulate (reappraise, distance, accept, or otherwise modulate emotional responses).

This is a task-based fMRI study of human youth viewing emotional (negative) faces vs shapes (implicit emotion processing), reports task-related brain activation and includes clinical and control groups; the meta-analysis objective explicitly admits studies that view emotional stimuli without regulation, so the study is eligible for full-text review.

Task-based fMRI with human participants (N=22) reporting task-related BOLD results; abstract suggests recruitment of emotion-regulation processes but does not clearly state participants were instructed to regulate. Inclusion uncertain on I2, so include for full-text review.

EXCLUDED because the study is a task-based fMRI with human participants and reports task-related activations (I1, I3, I4), but the abstract does not describe an emotion regulation task or instructions to regulate emotions (I2 not met). No exclusion criteria (E1, E2) apply.

No exclusion criteria met. Human participants are included (I3 met). Not a task-based fMRI activation study—uses resting-state functional connectivity after script-driven imagery (I1 not met). No explicit emotion-regulation task described (I2 not met). Does not report task-related activation results (I4 not met).

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study in interpersonal trauma survivors with PTSD and healthy controls, reporting relationships between affect and regional brain activation. Inclusion is uncertain regarding whether the task involves explicit emotion regulation versus passive/non-conscious emotional viewing and whether stimuli were visual; therefore include for full-text review.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants, ages included), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion not met: I2 - abstract does not describe an emotion-regulation instruction or strategy (it reports attentional modulation via an affective Stroop, not explicit regulation).

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study in adolescents examining brain responses to emotional words (I1, I3). It does not indicate participants performed an emotion-regulation task (I2 not demonstrated), and task-related activation reporting is not explicitly stated (I4 unclear). Insufficient information to determine whether an emotion-regulation paradigm was used, so include for full-text review.

No evidence the task was an emotion-regulation task: fMRI compared scratching/picking vs caressing (tactile stimulation) rather than instructed regulation of emotional responses to stimuli. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human clinical sample with control group), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion not met: I2 (no demonstrated emotion-regulation instructions or paradigm). Exclusion criteria: none met.

Task-based fMRI with human participants and task-related activation reported (I1, I3, I4). Abstract does not indicate an explicit emotion-regulation instruction or strategy (I2 unclear); study examines individual differences in external motivation during face evaluation. No exclusion criteria clearly met. Include for full-text review to determine whether an emotion-regulation task was used.

The study is a task-based fMRI experiment reporting task-related brain activation in 20 healthy women (I1, I3, I4 met). The abstract examines mood induction and affect-related brain responses but does not clearly state that participants were instructed to regulate their emotional responses (I2 unclear). No exclusion criteria appear to apply. Include for full-text review to determine whether an explicit emotion-regulation instruction/task was used.

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human clinical and control groups), I4 (reports task-related activation/connectivity). Inclusion criteria not met: I2 (no emotion regulation task — participants performed emotion discrimination/viewing rather than being instructed to regulate their emotional responses).

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human adolescent participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion IDs not met / not demonstrated: I2 (participants performing an emotion regulation task) — the abstract describes passive viewing of emotional stimuli with no regulation instructions. Does NOT meet I9 because the NeuroStore record labels the provided contrast as a between-group contrast ("negative > neutral [contrast, between-group]") and this study record contains only that analysis, so there is no clear within-group task contrast reported. Full-text exclusion E6 applies (reports only between-group contrasts with no within-group task effect).

NeuroStore record indicates a task-based fMRI Emotional Face Matching Task with visual stimuli (faces) and whole-brain, cluster-corrected results (I5, I7, I10, I11). Sample reporting meets inclusion (I8). However, the record does not describe any instructed emotion regulation strategy (no reappraisal or other regulation instruction) so I6 is not met, and the reported contrasts are described as a between-group interaction (face > shape; interaction, between-group) with no within-group regulation or passive viewing contrasts reported, so I9 is not met. Because the record shows only between-group/interaction contrasts with no within-group task effect, exclusion criterion E6 applies.

NeuroStore record indicates this is a resting-state seed-based connectivity study (Task: Rest Task; connectivity method seed based) rather than a task-based fMRI study with instructed emotion regulation of visual stimuli. The record shows no within-task emotion-regulation contrasts or task-evoked activation maps. Meets I8 (sample criteria) but does NOT meet I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation task), I7 (visual emotional stimuli), I9 (within-task regulation or passive viewing contrasts), or I10 (group-level whole-brain task activation maps). Exclusion E5 applies (reports only seed-based connectivity results / resting-state or connectivity analyses without task activation maps).

Meets I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli - headshots), I8 (appropriate sample), I9 (reports within-task contrasts e.g. acceptance>rejection), I10 (whole-brain voxelwise results with coordinates), and I11 (results clearly reported). Does NOT meet I6: there is no instruction to regulate emotion (no reappraisal or other regulation instruction reported); the task elicits affective responses to peer feedback but does not instruct emotion regulation. No full-text incompleteness indicated in the record.

The NeuroStore record indicates the task is passive viewing with no regulation instruction (fails I6) and all reported analyses are ROI-based with no whole-brain group-level voxelwise results (fails I10). This meets exclusion criterion E4 (ONLY ROI results reported). The record does show it is a task-based fMRI study with visual stimuli, an acceptable sample, and reports within-task viewing contrasts (I5, I7, I8, I9 met).

NeuroStore record shows this is an N-back task with emotionally salient distracting faces (I5, I7) and an appropriate sample (I8). However, the record does not describe any instructed emotion regulation strategy (I6 not met), does not report any within-group regulation or passive viewing contrasts (I9 not met), and all reported analyses are ROI-based rather than whole-brain voxelwise maps (I10 not met). Therefore the study appears to report ONLY region-of-interest results (E4) and ONLY between-group contrasts with no within-group task effects (E6), so it fails the full-text inclusion requirements.

The NeuroStore record shows a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study with visual stimuli and whole-brain peak coordinates (I5, I7, I10, I11). Sample meets inclusion (I8). However, the task was passive movie viewing with instructions to 'watch' and no regulation instructions, so the study does not meet I6 (no instructed emotion regulation). All reported contrasts are described as omnibus between-group contrasts (contrast: omnibus, between-group), and no within-group regulation or passive viewing contrasts are reported in the record, so I9 is not met. This also meets exclusion E6 (ONLY between-group contrasts or interactions with no within-group task effect).

Record shows a task-based whole-brain fMRI study with visual stimuli and healthy adult sample (meets I5, I7, I8, I10). However, the task instructions indicate passive viewing and rating of faces/photos (no instruction to regulate emotion), and the reported contrasts are prime x photo interactions rather than explicit regulation (reappraisal) or a clear unregulated viewing contrast. Therefore the study does not meet I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy) and does not clearly meet I9 (no explicit within-task regulation contrast or unregulated viewing contrast reported).

I5 Task-based fMRI: record shows an Affective Picture Viewing Task (event-related). I6 Emotion regulation strategy: The record does not explicitly state instruction to regulate (reappraisal), but task appears to be passive viewing with a target-probe; however, meta-analysis objective includes both regulate and view; still inclusion requires an instructed regulation strategy. The presence of within-task contrasts related to emotion (negative > positive) meets I9. I7 Visual stimuli: IAPS pictures meet criterion. I8 Sample: healthy adult females reported. I10 Whole-brain evidence: analysis is whole brain with MNI coordinates and reported peaks. The only possible missing item is I6 (explicit instruction to regulate) — the study seems to be about negativity bias, not reappraisal; however inclusion criteria allow unregulated viewing contrasts. Therefore study meets full-text criteria.

Meets I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli: face pictures), and I8 (sample reported including trauma and comparison youth). The NeuroStore record does NOT report any within-group whole-brain task activation contrasts (e.g. reappraise > look or emotion > baseline); instead it lists a group x condition interaction (between-group contrast) and a PPI connectivity result. Additionally, although spatial scope is labelled 'whole brain', the inference states 'FWE small-volume correction; corrected within roi', indicating results were reported with ROI small-volume correction rather than an unambiguous whole-brain voxelwise group map with reported peaks. Therefore the record fails I9 and I10 and meets exclusion criteria E4 (only ROI/SVC results reported) and E6 (only between-group/interaction contrasts reported).

The NeuroStore record describes an fMRI task (I5) using an instructed affect-labeling task (label emotion vs match emotion), which qualifies as an instructed emotion-regulation-related paradigm (I6: affect labeling is an incidental regulation strategy described in the abstract). Stimuli are visual faces (I7). Sample is healthy participants reported separately (I8). The analysis is a within-group task contrast related to labeling/regulation (label emotion > match emotion) (I9). The analysis is whole-brain with MNI coordinates and reported peaks (I10,I11). No exclusion criteria (E3-E7) are met based on the record.

The record indicates a task-based fMRI study with visual face stimuli and whole-brain group-level results (meets I5, I7, I8, I10). However, the task is an intentional empathy / perspective-taking instruction ('empathize with perceived emotional or neutral faces') rather than an instructed emotion-regulation strategy such as cognitive reappraisal (violates I6). The contrasts are empathy > baseline rather than explicit regulation or passive unregulated viewing contrasts required for this meta-analysis (I9 not met). This falls under exclusion E7 (empathy/perspective-taking without instruction to amplify or dampen one's own emotional response).

Record shows a task-based fMRI Cyberball social exclusion paradigm with visual stimuli (virtual players, ball) and block design (I5, I7). Sample includes both healthy controls and cocaine-dependent patients reported separately (I8). Analyses include within-task contrasts of social exclusion > inclusion (unregulated viewing) and whole-brain voxelwise results with MNI coordinates (I9, I10, I11). The record does not state any instructed emotion-regulation strategy (I6 not specified), but I9 allows unregulated viewing contrasts so the study still meets inclusion for this meta-analysis.

The NeuroStore record shows this is a task-based fMRI study with instructed regulation (attentional deployment) and within-task contrasts (I5, I6, I9). The sample qualifies (I8). However, the emotional stimuli reported for the key analyses are auditory (aversive sounds, musical pieces) rather than visual, so the required visual-stimulus criterion I7 is not met. Additionally, the shared metadata explicitly lists the spatial scope as 'region of interest' with FWE small-volume correction (ROI SVC) for all analyses, indicating no reported whole-brain voxelwise peaks; this fails I10 and meets exclusion E4 (only ROI/SVC results reported). The record does mention ROI-based and whole-brain t-tests in model lines, but the reported spatial scope and inference fields indicate only ROI-corrected results were reported. Full text appears readable (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The NeuroStore record describes a Posner spatial cueing task with monetary feedback and an omnibus between-group contrast. While the study is task-based (I5), uses visual stimuli (I7), reports whole-brain group results with coordinates (I10, I11), and has an eligible sample (I8), it does not describe an instructed emotion-regulation strategy (fails I6) and the reported contrast is a between-group omnibus contrast rather than a within-group regulation or passive viewing contrast (fails I9). No full-text exclusion criteria (E3-E7) are met by the record.

Meets I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual IAPS stimuli), I8 (sample includes BPD patients and healthy controls reported separately), I10 (at least one whole-brain group analysis reported: Analysis 27838143_analysis_2), and I11 (results reported as peaks/tables). Does NOT meet I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy: instructions were to judge whether picture was inside or outside, not to regulate emotion) and does NOT meet I9 (no within-task contrasts of regulation attempts or unregulated viewing reported; all listed analyses are between-group interactions or connectivity). Because the NeuroStore record shows only between-group contrasts/interactions and connectivity results with no within-group task effects, exclusion criterion E6 applies.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study with instructed emotion regulation (distraction) and within-task contrasts reported (I5, I6, I9, I8 met), the emotional stimuli are audiotaped narrative stories (auditory), not VISUAL stimuli (I7 not met). Additionally, all analyses are reported with spatial scope 'region of interest' and region-level inference, with no whole-brain voxelwise results reported (I10 not met). Therefore exclusion criterion E4 (ONLY ROI results with no whole-brain analysis) applies.

NeuroStore record describes an incidental emotional face processing fMRI task (gender ID), with no instruction to regulate emotions. Thus the study does not meet I6 (emotion regulation strategy instructed). The record does meet I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample), I9 (within-task emotion/viewing contrasts like habituation), I10 (whole-brain results with peak coordinates), and I11. No full-text exclusion criteria are met from the record.

The NeuroStore record describes a task-based fMRI study (I5) using visual facial stimuli (I7), with eligible participant sample reporting within-task contrasts of passive viewing (Angry > Neutral) (I9). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results with MNI coordinates are reported (I10, I11). The task instructions indicate gender identification with no explicit emotion-regulation instruction, so I6 (an instructed emotion-regulation task) is not met; however the meta-analysis objective permits unregulated viewing contrasts and I9 is satisfied, so the study is included.

All required full-text inclusion criteria are met based on the NeuroStore record: I5 task-based fMRI (event-related fMRI design), I6 an instructed emotion-regulation strategy (cognitive distraction during anticipation), I7 visual stimuli (IAPS pictures), I8 eligible sample (healthy participants reported separately), I9 within-task contrasts related to regulation and unregulated viewing (working-memory manipulation during anticipation and emotion contrasts), I10 whole-brain group-level voxelwise results reported with peak coordinates (Analyses 0 and 1 report whole-brain FWE-corrected peaks), I11 coordinate tables/figures acceptable. No full-text exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are met. The SVC noted for Analysis 2 does not negate the presence of other whole-brain analyses.

Record indicates a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs an emotion regulation strategy (attentional deployment; I6), uses visual stimuli (arrays of boxes and highlighted outcomes; I7), reports a qualifying sample (I8), includes within-task contrasts related to regulation and outcome processing (e.g., GF > MF; Opt > Nopt; I9), and provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with peak coordinates in MNI space (whole-brain FWE-corrected peaks; I10, I11). No full-text exclusion criteria from E3-E7 are met based on the record.

The NeuroStore record indicates a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructed cognitive control of emotional responses (incongruent AA trials require overriding automatic approach-avoidance, matching I6's 'instructed cognitive control'). Stimuli are visual faces (I7). Sample and reporting meet I8. The record reports within-task regulation-related contrasts (incongruent > congruent) and an unregulated viewing contrast (angry > happy) (I9). At least one group-level whole-brain analysis with peak coordinates is reported (Analyses 0 and 2) satisfying I10, and peaks are reported consistent with I11. No exclusion criteria (E3-E7) are indicated by the record.

Based on the NeuroStore record, this is a task-based fMRI study (I5) with a qualifying sample (I8). However, the reported analysis is an ROI-based correlation of Stroop (color-word) task responses with stress-related working memory changes and does not involve an instructed emotion-regulation task or emotional visual stimuli. Specifically, it fails I6 (no emotion-regulation instruction; task is cognitive Stroop), I7 (stimuli are color words, not emotional visual stimuli), I9 (no within-task emotion-regulation or unregulated emotional-viewing contrast is reported), and I10 (no whole-brain, voxelwise group-level map is reported; the analysis is ROI-based). Full-text exclusion E4 (ONLY ROI results reported) therefore applies.

Record indicates a task-based fMRI study with visual stimuli (clips of participants' children) and reports within-task whole-brain contrasts (Own > Stranger) with coordinates (meets I5, I7, I9, I10, I8). However, the NeuroStore record does not state that an emotion regulation strategy was instructed (no mention of reappraisal, increase/decrease, distancing, or other regulation instructions), so the required inclusion criterion I6 is not met. No full-text exclusion criteria from the list are met.

The NeuroStore record describes an Ultimatum Game decision-making fMRI study with whole-brain results, but it does not indicate that participants were instructed to use an emotion regulation strategy (e.g. reappraisal) or that any contrasts reflect passive unregulated viewing of emotional visual stimuli. Thus I6 (instruction to regulate) and I9 (a within-task emotion-regulation or unregulated viewing contrast) are not met. Coordinate space is listed as OTHER rather than a standard anatomical space, so I10 (peak coordinates in a standard space) is also not clearly met from the record. The record does clearly meet I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), and I8 (acceptable sample). No exclusion criteria E3–E7 are indicated by the record.

The NeuroStore record describes a task-based fMRI study (I5) using an instructed regulation-like manipulation (No-Think instructions to prevent scenes from coming to mind) that the abstract frames as regulating emotional content (I6). Stimuli are visual (I7: IAPS scenes). Sample and design meet inclusion (I8). The record reports within-task contrasts contrasting regulation versus retrieval (No-Think > Think; Think > No-Think) (I9). At least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis with peak coordinates is reported (Analyses 0 and 1; I10,I11). No full-text exclusion criteria from E3–E7 are indicated by the record. Note: the regulation strategy is retrieval suppression rather than classic reappraisal; I6 is judged met because the study explicitly frames suppression as regulating emotional content.

The NeuroStore record shows this is a task-based fMRI study with visual stimuli (I5, I7), an acceptable sample (I8), reports a within-task unregulated viewing contrast (separation > play) (I9), and provides whole-brain voxelwise results with coordinates (I10, I11). However, the record does NOT indicate any instructed emotion regulation strategy (I6) — instructions state only to 'View silent video excerpts', i.e. passive viewing. Because I6 (an instructed regulation task) is not met, the study does not satisfy all required inclusion criteria.

The NeuroStore record shows an fMRI Ultimatum Game task with visual stimuli (NimStim faces) and BOLD measures (I5, I7, I8 met). However the record does NOT indicate that an emotion-regulation strategy was instructed (I6 not met), does not report any within-task regulation or unregulated viewing contrasts (no reappraisal/decrease/increase/maintain contrasts are described; I9 not met), and the only explicitly described statistical result is a region-of-interest analysis (Analysis 29309499_analysis_3: spatial scope=ROI), with no clear whole-brain, group-level voxelwise maps reported in the record (I10 not met). Therefore the study does not meet the full set of inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

Task-based fMRI with visual emotional face stimuli (I5, I7). The task includes affect labeling which is an instructed emotion-focused task (treated here as an instructed emotion-regulation strategy), meeting I6. Sample and groups meet I8. Multiple analyses include within-task contrasts relevant to regulation or viewing (I9). Several analyses report whole-brain group-level results with peak coordinates in tables (I10,I11).

Record describes a task-based fMRI emotion regulation study using visual IAPS stimuli with instructed up-regulation (meets I5, I6, I7). Sample includes MDD patients and healthy controls (meets I8). However, the only reported analysis is a seed-based generalized PPI connectivity result reported as a between-group interaction (CON increase > MDD view), with whole-brain connectivity inference; no within-group task activation contrasts or whole-brain univariate activation maps are reported in the NeuroStore record. Therefore the study reports ONLY connectivity results (E5) and only a between-group interaction with no within-group task effect (E6), so it fails I9 and I10 and must be excluded.

The NeuroStore record indicates a task-based fMRI study (I5) using instructed emotion regulation (increase/enhance and suppress) consistent with cognitive reappraisal (I6). Stimuli are visual IAPS images (I7). Sample includes depressed patients with separate reporting (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts/ regressions related to regulation/sustained activity (I9). At least one group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task analysis with peak coordinates is reported (Analyses 3 and 4) satisfying whole-brain evidence (I10,I11). No full-text exclusion criteria from the provided record apply.

The NeuroStore record shows this is a task-based fMRI study (I5) with an acceptable sample (I8). However, it does NOT meet key inclusion criteria: I6 (no emotion regulation instruction - the task is a Parametric Go/No-Go with letters, not a regulation task), I7 (stimuli are letters, not emotional visual stimuli), I9 (the reported contrast is a between-group omnibus, not a within-task emotion regulation or passive viewing contrast), and I10 (the result is reported as a region-of-interest analysis rather than a whole-brain voxelwise map). The record therefore meets exclusion criteria E4 (reports only ROI results) and E6 (reports only between-group contrast/interaction with no within-group task effect).

I5 met: task-based fMRI (Threat-of-Shock / Threat Anticipation). I6 NOT met: no emotion regulation strategy is instructed in the task record—the task describes anticipation of shock and safe conditions but contains no instruction to regulate emotion (reappraisal or other strategies). I7 met: stimuli are visual (shock and safe conditions displayed on a screen). I8 met: sample includes patients and healthy participants (ages reported). I9 met: analyses report within-task contrasts related to emotional responding (shock > safe, safe > shock). I10 met: whole-brain voxelwise results reported with MNI coordinates. I11 met: coordinate tables reported. Excluded because full-text inclusion criterion I6 (instructed emotion regulation) is not satisfied by the record.

The NeuroStore record describes an fMRI perceptual-judgment task with visual stimuli and reports within-task contrasts (bodies>scrambled, faces>scrambled) including whole-brain results. However, the record does not indicate any instructed emotion-regulation strategy (e.g. reappraisal/decrease/increase) or instruction to regulate during anticipation or stimulus presentation. Therefore full-text inclusion criterion I6 (an emotion regulation strategy is instructed) is not met. Other inclusion criteria (I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, I11) are met based on the record. No full-text exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are indicated by the record.

Study is an fMRI task study with visual stimuli and an eligible sample (I5, I7, I8). However, the NeuroStore record does not indicate any instructed emotion-regulation strategy (I6 not met) and reports only between-group omnibus contrasts/interactions and connectivity analyses with no within-group task contrasts isolating regulation or passive viewing (I9 not met). The analyses are whole-brain (I10 met), but because the paper reports only between-group/interaction contrasts and connectivity with no within-group regulation or passive-viewing contrasts, it meets exclusion criterion E6. Full text appears accessible from the record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The NeuroStore record shows this is a task-based fMRI study with whole-brain, voxelwise results reported in MNI space and an eligible sample (meets I5, I8, I10). However, the reported stimuli are individual adjectives (word stimuli), which are explicitly excluded by I7 (word/sentence stimuli are non-qualifying). The record does not indicate any instructed emotion regulation strategy (no reappraisal or other regulation instruction), so I6 is not met. The extracted analyses are reported as BETWEEN-GROUP interactions (LTM > MNP for SC>NT and SP>NT) and the record lists no within-group task contrasts; thus the study appears to report ONLY between-group contrasts with no within-group task effect (meets exclusion E6). Because I6 and I7 (and I9, no within-group contrasts) are not met and E6 applies, the study is excluded.

execution_stats.search_query: ((("functional magnetic resonance imaging"[tiab] OR "functional MRI"[tiab] OR fMRI[tiab] OR neuroimaging[tiab] OR "Magnetic Resonance Imaging"[Mesh] OR "Brain Mapping"[Mesh]) AND ("emotion regulation"[tiab] OR "affective regulation"[tiab] OR reappraisal[tiab])) AND ("2000/01/01"[Date - Publication] : "2019/12/31"[Date - Publication])) NOT (Editorial[pt] OR Letter[pt] OR Comment[pt] OR "Case Reports"[pt] OR News[pt] OR Review[pt])
